viii. Expectations for infrastructure funds and capacity building
Overview of infrastructure funding: OHIP expects SCNs to support capacity building for CBOs within the
Network. SCN Lead Entities will receive infrastructure funding to support development of the Network.
Infrastructure funds are used directly by the SCN Lead Entity and distributed to CBOs (CBO capacity building
funds). SCN Lead Entities are prohibited from distributing any form of infrastructure funding in the form of a gift
card.

Use of infrastructure funding for onboarding to the SCN IT Platform and technical assistance: SCNs should use
infrastructure funding to assist entities that are contracted with the SCN to provide access and onboarding to
the IT platform and training. In addition to funding, SCN Lead Entities are responsible for providing onboarding
support to contracted organizations in the Network for the following topics as needed:

    •   Setting up and using the SCN IT Platform
    •   Conducting HRSN Screenings using the AHC HRSN Screening Tool
    •   Completing Eligibility Assessments and Social Care Plan development
    •   Tracking referrals, service provision, and service completion
    •   Ongoing technical assistance

Capacity building funds for CBOs
[[p.38]]
Distribution and eligibility for CBO capacity building funds: CBO capacity building funds may only be distributed
by SCN Lead Entities to not-for-profit 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) charitable organizations that work at the local level
to meet community needs and provide HRSN waiver services to members. SCN Lead Entities will determine
distribution of capacity building funding across eligible CBOs that meet this definition. SCN Lead Entities should
ensure that CBO capacity building funding is distributed to build CBO capacity across a diverse set of CBOs in the
Network. Information on capacity funding and its uses should be shared with CBOs upon initial engagement or
shared alongside information about joining the Network. Capacity dollars including incentive funding, uses of
funding, and relevant metrics related to the capacity funds must be outlined either in the SCN- HRSN Service
Provider agreement or in a separate agreement between the SCN and CBO.

OHIP strongly encourages SCN Lead Entities to create efficient, accessible processes to distribute capacity
building funding to CBOs (e.g., sharing clear information on requirements to obtain capacity building funding at
the start of the contracting process, using a simple application with clear criteria for receipt of funding).

Lead Entities may choose to make a portion of a CBO's capacity building funding award contingent on CBO
operations / performance to encourage CBO scale-up (e.g., contingent on the achievement of certain
milestones).

OHIP requirements for uses and tracking of funds (outlined in Table 7-1 Allowable uses of infrastructure funding
and eligible organizations) apply to all funds distributed to Lead Entities, regardless of whether funding is
contingent on performance.

Health systems or other health care providers as defined in this Manual, clinics, behavioral health clinics,
federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs), MCOs, local
departments of health, and for-profit entities are NOT eligible for CBO capacity building funds but may be
eligible for capacity building funds for healthcare providers and behavioral health providers (see below for more
information). Health Homes run through FQHCs, behavioral health clinics, and health systems are eligible for
CBO capacity building funds, as long as the Health Home meets the criteria outlined below.

Health Homes and Care Coordination Organizations

Health Homes and Care Coordination Organizations (CCOs) may receive capacity building funds if the following
criteria are met:

    •   They have a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status and either of the following:
           a. They have a separate line of business that will provide HRSN Services which is operated in a
               separate division or unit from the portion of the business that is billing for Health Home
               Services; the line of business providing HRSN services must have separate books and records,
               staff, and management from the Health Homes business or are contracted with a SCN to receive
               referrals outside of the Health Home members from the SCN; or
           b. Health Homes and CCOs may receive capacity building funds to hire, onboard, provide
               equipment to, and train full or part-time staff (Social Care Navigators) if they provide Screening,
               Navigation and Enhanced Care Management to Health Home/CCO members and non-Health
               Home members that meet the enhanced (level 2) eligibility criteria
[[p.39]]
In general, Health Homes and CCOs may apply for capacity building funds on behalf of the separate line of
business providing HRSN Services. The line of business that receives and uses the funds must use the funds
towards delivering HRSN Services to members. This includes Health Homes run through FQHCs, behavioral
health clinics, and health systems as long as the Health Home meets the above criteria. Care management
agencies may receive capacity funding if they have a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status.

Allowable use of CBO capacity building funds: Allowable uses of funds for capacity building include direct
funding to non-profit organizations, such as:
    • Onboarding, training, and salaries for full- or part-time staff who provide services (e.g., conducting
        outreach to members, providing screenings & navigation)
    • Procuring equipment or technology required to launch or scale services
    • Investing in office space or operational needs tied directly to service delivery

Enabling program planning and development directly related to enhanced HRSN services CBOs may receive both
capacity building funds as well as payments for the delivery of HRSN services to individual members.

OHIP encourages SCNs to use the following practices with regard to distribution of capacity building funding to
CBOs:
   • Providing upfront funds to cover time related to training, equipment, and start-up expenses
   • Allowing up to 12 months of salary and fringe for FTEs dedicated to the SCN HRSN Services as the
       volume of service payments ramps up
   • Assisting CBOs with calculating how the referral volume and rate will sustain staffing and overhead

SCNs are expected to report components of their CBO capacity building in the Infrastructure Cost Report (See
SCN Reporting).

Capacity building funding for healthcare providers (HCPs) and behavioral health providers

SCNs may distribute infrastructure funds to healthcare providers—including hospitals, health systems, physician
offices, FQHCs, and behavioral health providers—to hire FTE Social Care Navigators. The purpose of this funding
is to increase the number of Medicaid members in different care settings with access to HRSN services.

Capacity building funds may be used for the salary and fringe benefits of an FTE Social Care Navigator who solely
works on the SCN program. These FTEs must be trained and onboarded onto the SCN IT Platform. SCNs will only
fund providers who serve high-needs populations in underserved communities (e.g., using hotspot data) and
whose patient population consists of at least 30% Medicaid members within their practice. Navigators must
conduct screenings, eligibility assessments, make referrals, and provide Enhanced Care Management to
members. Providers are also permitted to use their EHR to conduct the AHC screening, or AHC Embedded Tool,
and within the same day have the navigator provide the members assessment and referral in the SCN IT
Platform. The Navigators are required to meet the SCN’s goals and metrics as criteria for receiving funding.
Funding may also be used as incentive or bonus payments for meeting metrics and goals set by the SCN.

Providers participating in the Medicaid Hospital Global Budget Initiative are not eligible to receive capacity
building funds. Documentation requirements for healthcare provider capacity building funds align with those of
CBO capacity building funds.

sections.title: Governance Requirements
sections.text:
b. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS
Both when SCNs are initially launched and as they grow and mature over time, it is essential that SCN Lead
Entities have a way to receive feedback from Network members and other community partners, align on shared
priorities and strategic goals, and collaboratively make or approve important operational decisions. To achieve
this, SCN LEs must issue the OHIP-provided, “HRSN Service Provider Survey” to their network on an annual basis
and share the final survey results with OHIP and their governing body for discussion, improvement, and
resolution of issues. The survey is due to OHIP at the end of April every calendar year.

To ensure that all SCNs have clear structures in place to meet those needs, OHIP requires that each SCN Lead
Entity create a governing body for its region. Governing bodies should be comprised of a wide array of
stakeholders in the region, including (but not limited to) CBOs delivering HRSN services, providers, advocacy
organizations, members, and other community members who are representative of the communities served by
the SCN. CBOs should comprise the majority of the governing board for each SCN.

To better understand and address disparities and inequities that can impact Medicaid members’ HRSNs and
their ability to access HRSN services, OHIP expects SCN Lead Entities to ensure their governing bodies include a
broad and regionally representative group of individuals with diverse backgrounds and identities with regard to
race, ethnicity, age, disability status, and socioeconomic status.

Before the start of service delivery, the SCN Lead Entity must define a governing body that includes:

    •   Community based organizations providing HRSN services in the SCN’s region. CBOs must represent at
        least 51% (excluding the SCN Lead Entity) of the governing body and have a majority share of voting
        rights. CBOs must have a service location in the SCN region in order to qualify for this requirement. A
        CBO may serve on multiple different SCN Governing boards if they provide services in multiple SCN
        regions
    •   Health care and care management providers (e.g., health systems, providers, FQHCs, behavioral health
        (BH) providers, local health departments, Health Homes) in the SCN region, and including at least one
        provider with mental health and Substance Use Disorder (SUD) experience is preferred
    •   Community advocates who are collectively representative of the region and who the SCN serves
    •   Current Medicaid members, including at least two current Medicaid members with experience receiving
        HRSN services and/or HRSN Social Care Navigation. Note that SCN Lead Entities are not expected to post
        publicly the names of Medicaid members participating in the SCN Governing Body. Medicaid member
        names may be posted publicly only if members provide permission, but they should not be identified as
        a Medicaid member

The SCN Lead Entity will also need to ensure that the governing body follows any requirements for the
governing bodies of 501(c)(3) organizations and is convened in routine intervals, at least quarterly.
[[p.41]]
Figure 4-1: Requirements for composition of members of SCN Lead Entity governing body

sections.title: SCN IT Platform Requirements
sections.text:
c. SCN IT PLATFORM REQUIREMENTS

i. Introduction to Platform Requirements
For an SCN to truly serve as an interconnected Network that identifies and addresses HRSNs, many kinds of data
and information need to be shared across organizations.

For example, imagine a primary care provider has a patient who is a current Medicaid member with complex
health conditions. They screen the member for HRSNs and learn that they are food insecure. The provider needs
to share those Screening results with the SCN. A Social Care Navigator within the SCN needs to review the
Screening and conduct an Eligibility Assessment to determine whether the member is eligible to receive
Enhanced HRSN Services. Once the Social Care Navigators determines the member is eligible, they will need to
refer to the appropriate HRSN service provider who can provide the right HRSN service. The HRSN service
provider who receives that referral needs to know what HRSN services the member is eligible to receive. The
SCN Lead Entity needs to pay the HRSN service provider for delivering the service. OHIP needs to know what
services were provided and whether they impacted the member’s health outcomes and costs.

For that information to be exchanged in a seamless and timely way, it is critical that each SCN has a shared
technology infrastructure that allows organizations in the Network to send and receive information.

Rather than mandate the use of a specific technology platform, OHIP is giving SCN Lead Entities the flexibility to
each implement an SCN IT Platform that is the best fit for their region’s needs. SCN IT Platforms will all be
required to have certain features and meet specific requirements described in this section.
[[p.42]]
As SCNs will be comprised of a wide variety of organizations, with varying levels of administrative capacity and
experience with similar technology, OHIP encourages SCN Lead Entities to prioritize creating a platform that can
provide an easy, intuitive, and efficient user experience for the Network.

ii. Platform Functionality
One comprehensive platform or seamless integration of multiple technologies: All SCN Lead Entities must have
an SCN IT Platform that enables core responsibilities of the SCN, including Screening, Eligibility Assessment,
Navigation, Network management, and fiscal management.

To achieve this, SCN Lead Entities have the flexibility to take either of two different approaches to providing a
SCN IT Platform for their region:

    1. Contract with one comprehensive SCN IT Platform that meets all technical and functional requirements
       in a single system
    2. Contract or subcontract with multiple technologies / systems that collectively meet all technical and
       functional requirements and are seamlessly integrated and managed centrally

Each SCN Lead Entity must ensure that its SCN IT Platform has the capability to meet the requirements of the
Key Product Features below. If an SCN’s IT Platform does not meet those requirements, the SCN Lead Entity
should meet with OHIP to establish a plan to address any unmet requirements, which may include the use of a
different platform to meet the requirement of the NYHER program.

iii. Key Product Features of SCN IT Platforms:
Please note additional details may be found in the Platform Resource Pack.

Member information: Display member information (e.g., member contact information, member’s MCO details)
and eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services. Member information displayed should vary depending on users’
authorization level

User roles, access, and compliance:

    •   Different organizations in the SCN require unique user roles based on their responsibilities. This is often
        referred to as “Role Based Access Controls.” The SCN Lead Entity is required to manage SCN IT Platform
        user roles, including assigning appropriate levels of access and responsibility within the SCN IT Platform.
        Users should only have access to the minimum necessary information to perform their tasks as assigned
        Examples:
            o The HRSN service provider providing a service does not need the same level of access as a Social
                 Care Navigator performing an Eligibility Assessment where they may need access to sensitive
                 health information to determine Eligibility. An HRSN service provider installing handrails doesn’t
                 necessarily need information about diagnoses and eligibility status; the service provider only
                 needs enough information to install handrails that meet the need of that Medicaid member
            o The HRSN service provider also does not need access to information about Medicaid members
                 for whom it does not provide case services
    •   The SCN Lead Entity must ensure users are verified against unique identifiers and access control is
        limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the necessary tasks (e.g., Eligibility Assessment)
[[p.43]]
    •   The SCN Lead Entity will also ensure that SCN IT Platform users have met Screening / referral training
        requirements

Screening:

    •   Enable users to screen members using a standardized embedded Screening Tool (i.e., AHC HRSN
        Screening Tool, AHC Embedded Tool), enable near-real time member-level updates to Screening status,
        and results. The Platform should also be able to capture and track member consent
            o Support terminology and the minimum viable data set
            o Exhibit FHIR competency

Eligibility Assessment:

    •   Enable a user to determine member eligibility for receiving Enhanced HRSN Services by ensuring logic
        from Table 5-13, Table 5-14, Table 5-15, and Table 5-16 is automated for Eligibility Assessments and
        Navigation workflows. The SCN IT Platform must apply this logic for eligibility criteria for enhanced
        populations, clinical criteria, and Social Risk Factors to offer a timely and efficient user experience that
        limits options for referrals only to the HRSN domain and applicable sub-services the member is eligible
        for and addresses the member’s identified unmet HRSN. Based on the unmet need screened and the
        Eligibility Assessment, the platform should suggest appropriate HRSN service providers. For example,
             o If a member is not eligible for any Enhanced HRSN Services, no enhanced service providers
                  should be displayed
             o If a member is only eligible for Medically Tailored Meals, only Nutrition providers that provide
                  that particular service should come up
    •   Enhanced HRSN Services are for Medicaid Managed Care members in an Enhanced Population that have
        an identified unmet HRSN and wish to receive services
    •   Members with an identified unmet HRSN who are not eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services may be
        navigated to existing federal, state, and local services. Navigation to existing services may be completed
        for both Medicaid FFS and Medicaid Managed Care members that do not meet the criteria for Enhanced
        HRSN Services. Members who are eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services may also be navigated to existing
        federal, state, and local services
    •   The SCN IT Platform should also be able to capture and track member attestation for the accuracy of
        information provided throughout the Eligibility Assessment
    •   The SCN IT platform must retain all historical member data within the system for at minimum 10 years,
        including any initiated, partially completed or completed Eligibility Assessments, unless intentionally
        changed or deleted by the SCN Lead Entity or their contracted Social Care Navigators

Closed Loop Referrals for Enhanced HRSN Services:

    •   A Closed Loop Referral means that the Social Care Navigator who referred a member for Enhanced
        HRSN Services can see the status of the referral and knows whether the service was provided. The SCN
        IT Platform must conduct and manage Closed Loop Referrals and service coordination with HRSN service
        providers. This includes tracking:
                 o Enhanced HRSN Services a member is referred to
                 o Which HRSN service provider the referral was sent to and who has accepted the referral
                 o Status of the referral (e.g., open, closed)
                 o Time to Closed Loop Referral
[[p.44]]
                o    Details on services delivered (e.g., type of intervention, duration)

Coordination of health and social care:

    •   Allow input of notes to support service coordination by health and social care professionals (e.g., Social
        Care Navigators, case managers, providers)

Licenses:

    •   The SCN Lead Entity will obtain licenses for all participating entities including MCOs, providers, and
        HRSN service providers

Payment and fiscal administration:

    •   Draw upon each SCN’s HRSN Fee Schedule for services delivered, enable generation of social care
        claims, and track reimbursements

Performance management:

    •   Generate supporting information (e.g., performance dashboards) for SCN quarterly performance
        reporting requirements to OHIP and enable continuous improvement activities across SCNs

Data sharing and exchange:

    •   Facilitate bi-directional exchange of data with SHIN-NY (which will play a central role in SCN program
        operations) and enable near real-time data sharing across key program stakeholders. SCN IT Platforms
        should be able to incorporate eligibility files from MCOs via the SHIN-NY and into the SCN IT Platform to
        support the Eligibility Assessment process. (For 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability Guidance, SCN Lead
        Entities and their SCN IT Platform partners can access this information at
        https://www.nyehealth.org/1115-waiver/)
    •   Include support terminology and the minimum viable data
    •   Exhibit FHIR competency

iv. Background on Coding Granularity

nature of Navigation support provided and specific Enhanced HRSN services to which members are referred.

Per the Social Care Coding document, OHIP recognizes that this coding will require additional time for Social
Care Navigators to input. Accurately coding Navigation activities and HRSN service referrals is critical for both
SCNs and OHIP to conduct ongoing monitoring of SCN activities, including accurately tracking referrals to and
spend on various services, and to enable long-term program sustainability. In addition, granular coding will
enable evaluation of the impact of the SCN program and inform design of subsequent HRSN programs and risk
scoring methodology.

Wherever possible, OHIP encourages SCNs and SCN IT Platform vendors to automate filtering logic by only
having relevant coding available based on previous steps in the workflow to ensure time required from Social
Care Navigators is minimized.

v. Data Sharing - Interoperability
For HRSN data to be efficiently shared across many organizations and entities, it is important for there to be
common data standards (e.g., shared terminology and coding, shared data quality expectations) and
interoperability between any systems that are sending and receiving SCN data.

SCN Lead Entity responsibilities include:

    •   Agree to share data elements as defined in the minimum viable data set with the QE and send data to
        the QE who will then submit data on behalf of the SCN Lead Entity to the NYeC/SHIN-NY data lake
    •   In coordination with a QE, establish a user process and technical means to obtain data from the SHIN-NY
        via a real-time API call to the SHIN-NY data lake
    •   Ensure the SCN IT Platform vendor can display Medicaid member files and flag eligibility (e.g., member
        information, Enhanced Services eligibility)

    •   Ensure SCN IT Platform ability to submit Social Care Claims to MCO in a format that meets HIPAA post-

    •   Meet HL7 FHIR national standards for bi-directional data sharing and data transactions between the SCN
        Lead Entity and QE in accordance with 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability Guidance
    •   Define approach to aligning data quality standards and validation processes with existing federal and
        state data standards

For detailed requirements, see Data Sharing – Interoperability

vi. Data Governance, Privacy, and Security
In accordance with the participation agreements established among key stakeholders—including the SCN Lead
Entity and regional QE, as well as the SCN Lead Entity and MCO—all participating entities are mandated to
adhere to the SHIN-NY data privacy and governance policies and guidelines issued by OHIP.

(For detailed requirements, see Data Governance, Privacy, and Security)

sections.title: Training Expectations
sections.text:
d. TRAINING EXPECTATIONS
SCN Lead Entities are responsible for ensuring that all SCN employees, HRSN service providers, other entities in
the Network, and MCOs (if MCOs choose to participate in Screening, Eligibility Assessments, and / or Navigation)
are appropriately trained to serve Medicaid members either through trainings provided by the SCN Lead Entity
or through other means. SCN Lead Entities are expected to develop specific and comprehensive curricula that
are responsive to the needs of their population. They can also enlist vendors to meet these needs or use train
the trainer models.

Training should be relevant to the contracted provider’s role within the Network (e.g., Screening, Navigation,
HRSN service provision). Individuals, health care providers, behavioral health providers or specialized CBOs can
opt out of a training if they can attest that they have already taken or provided the needed training. The training
modality is at the SCN Lead Entity's discretion. Trainings, materials, and presentations must be able to
accommodate individuals with communication disabilities (e.g., vision, hearing, speech) when requested.

The length of time it takes to complete trainings provided by an SCN Lead Entity for an individual should not
exceed 30 days. SCN Lead Entities should ensure entities in their Network receive and complete training across
the following topics as relevant for each stakeholder:

The following two trainings are required as part of the onboarding process.

    •   Technology training: Instruction on how to use the SCN Lead Entity’s SCN IT Platform (including to MCOs
        if the MCO chooses to utilize the SCN IT Platform) – not applicable if using an independent platform for
        Screening
    •   Care delivery functions: Instruction on the Care Delivery Approach outlined in this Operations Manual
        should be determined by the SCN Lead Entity in consideration of the contracted role and service an
        individual will be providing

The following training is required, but entities can be onboarded and start providing services prior to
completion.
[[p.50]]
    •   Cultural and linguistic training: Instruction on being responsive to members’ diverse beliefs, practices,
        communication disabilities (e.g. vision, hearing or speech) and needs (For additional details on ensuring
        appropriate language access, see HRSN Network Capacity and Access)
    •   Trauma-informed training: Instruction on the impact of trauma and how to integrate trauma-informed
        approaches in work with vulnerable populations
    •   Members experiencing interpersonal safety concerns (IPS) training– training may include how to work
        with members who disclose IPS as well as an understanding of the SCN’s internal protocol on how to
        safely address IPS matters. In lieu of all Social Care Navigators having this training, there should be an
        escalation process with a staff member available that does have this training.
    •   Optional based on need - Population-specific training: Instruction on engaging with specific
        subpopulations including but not limited to:
            o Children and families, including those involved with foster care or child welfare systems
            o Members with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (I/DD)
            o Members with Behavioral Health conditions, including Serious Mental Illness (SMI) and
                Substance Use Disorders (SUD). Trainings should include policies on de-escalation techniques.
            o Criminal justice-involved populations, including justice-involved youth

Child abuse and neglect: OHIP expects SCN LEs to ensure Screeners, Social Care Navigators and Enhanced HRSN
service providers working with children and youth in their Network undertake appropriate training and/or equip
Social Care Navigators to report child abuse or neglect, as needed. Social Care Navigators are expected to report
or cause a report to be made when they have a reasonable cause to suspect that a child is abused or neglected.
Social Care Navigators who interact with children/youth and families must take the 2-hour web-based online
training course: New York State Mandated Reporter Resource Center - Home (nysmandatedreporter.org) SCN
Lead Entities must also provide their Conflict of Interest (COI) Plan to their Network and any necessary trainings
to implement and action on their COI Plan.

Reporting on training expectations: SCN Lead Entities will have the opportunity to report on training activities
to date in the Network Composition Plan and Report as well as the Quarterly Performance Report (Narrative) (for
more details on reporting guidelines, see SCN Reporting). SCN Lead Entities, prompted and facilitated by OHIP,
may also be asked to share their best practices across regions. OHIP reserves the right to adjust training
requirements and guidelines.
sections.change_note: Added guidance on providing training in an accessible format when needed, and new Interpersonal Safety (IPS) training guidance.

sections.title: SCN Public Website
sections.text:
e. SCN PUBLIC WEBSITE
The SCN Lead Entity will provide and maintain a public website capable of offering Screening and providing
information on the Network on or before January 1, 2025, as indicated in the SCN Lead Entity’s contract with
OHIP.

The SCN public website is expected to include:

    •   Basic introduction to SCN and services offered: Guidance to public audience on services provided by the
        SCN and member eligibility
    •   Enhanced Population criteria, clinical criteria and social risk factors for Enhanced HRSN Services:
        Information should either match or directly link to information posted on the DOH website under “HRSN
        Services Eligibility Summary”
[[p.51]]
    •   Complaint form for members and public entities: SCNs must maintain a complaint submission form
        on the main page of their SCN program website that is accessible to both Medicaid members and public
        entities. The complaint section must clearly state that the SCN will respond to and resolve the complaint
        within 45 calendar days of receipt and must also provide the email address or phone number of the
        entity responsible for follow-up.
    •   Contact information to reach SCN: SCN should include methods to reach the SCN (e.g., email, phone)
        and include guidance for the following two audiences that may try to contact the SCN:
             o Organizations seeking to reach the SCN (e.g., HRSN service providers, health care providers,
                 MCOs, other entities)
             o Members seeking to reach the SCN (e.g., seeking Screening information, support with accessing
                 SCN resources)
    •   Network organization directory: Up-to-date, publicly available SCN directory that includes all contracted
        HRSN service providers (see SCN Reporting for details on data elements that must be included in the
        quarterly Network Composition Report)
    •   HRSN Screening locations: Relevant contact information for each Screening location (e.g., address,
        hours, languages spoken, Screening modalities offered, etc.)
    •   Self-Screening capability: AHC HRSN Screening tool, or AHC Embedded Tool, for members to conduct a
        Self-Screen must be available on the SCN website, and SCNs could consider placing a link to the Self-
        Screening tool on the SCN website’s landing page so it is easy to access for members (i.e., members
        should not have to click through multiple pages to find the link to the Self-Screening tool). As a best
        practice, self-screening tools should pull the following data elements into the platform: member’s full
        name, phone numbers, date of birth and identification number; name and TIN/NPI of entity completing
        the self-screening tool; and name of person completing self-screening tool (if not member) and
        relationship to member
    •   Language translation: It is up to the discretion of the SCN Lead Entity to determine languages in which
        key information on the SCN website will be made available. OHIP encourages SCNs to make materials
        available in the languages that are common and preferred by Medicaid populations of the region (see
        HRSN Network Capacity and Access)
    •   Governing body: The SCN Lead Entity shall post a list of Governing Body members on the SCN website.
        SCN Lead Entities are not expected to post publicly the names of Medicaid members participating in the
        Governing Body. Medicaid member names may be posted publicly only if members provide permission,
        but they should not be identified as a Medicaid member. Additional details (e.g., meeting minutes) do
        not need to be posted on the website (see Governance Requirements)

Process for HRSN service provider & Ecosystem Partner complaints: The SCN shall publish how stakeholders
can submit complaints (related to exclusion from the SCN, issues with payments, etc.) to OHIP. For additional
details, see Section HRSN service provider & Ecosystem Partner Complaints.

In addition to the including the components above, SCN Lead Entities should ensure their Public Website is
designed with appropriate accessibility considerations. Accessibility considerations may include descriptive text
for hyperlinks, color contrast, embedded documents, appropriately descriptive text for resources, etc. In
addition, the Public Website should strive to communicate information in an easy-to-understand format (e.g.,
leveraging lists when appropriate, appropriate sub-headings, and tables for tabular information, etc.).
sections.change_note: SCNs must make their public complaint process visible on the site's main page and accessible.

sections.title: Public Materials on SCN Program
sections.text:
f. PUBLIC MATERIALS ON SCN PROGRAM
OHIP has provided SCN Lead Entities with marketing material such as factsheets / explainers and example media
(e.g., social media, videos) to help SCNs raise awareness and educate members, HRSN service providers, health
care providers (inclusive of behavioral health providers), and other stakeholders about how to engage with
SCNs.

To encourage consistent messaging and ensure accuracy, OHIP asks SCNs to leverage OHIP-developed materials
in recruiting providers and engaging members (found here on OHIP’s SCN page). The marketing toolkits provided
have clear direction on areas for customization and co-branding.

All marketing materials that will be shared with members and/or the community require OHIP approval.
Materials internal to the SCN Lead Entity’s Network (i.e., internal training materials, CBO guidelines) do not need
OHIP approval.

sections.title: Introduction (Care Delivery Approach)
sections.text:
a. INTRODUCTION
Core responsibilities of SCNs: OHIP’s overarching vision for the SCN program is to build comprehensive
statewide infrastructure that enables a consistent end-to-end process for identifying unmet HRSNs, connecting
members with unmet HRSNs to services, delivering effective HRSN services, and reimbursing HRSN service
providers.
Towards that vision, SCNs are responsible for administering a core set of responsibilities using standardized
processes, tools, and partnerships to ensure consistency and equity in how HRSNs are identified and addressed
at scale across regions and across many different HRSN service providers.

The core responsibilities of SCNs are:

    a)      Screen Medicaid members for HRSNs in a standardized and person-centered way using the AHC HRSN
            Screening Tool or AHC Embedded Tool
    b)      Conduct Eligibility Assessments for members whose Screening identifies unmet HRSNs and who
            request support. Eligibility Assessments will determine whether the member is eligible for Enhanced
            HRSN Services (Medicaid Managed Care members only) and/or existing federal, state, and local
            programs (e.g., SNAP, WIC, TANF)
    c)      Navigate members appropriately, including referring eligible members to Enhanced HRSN Services or
            navigating members to existing federal, state, and local services
    d)      Deliver Enhanced HRSN Services to eligible MMC members
    e)      Develop Social Care Plans that detail member HRSNs for eligible MMC members
    f)      Monitor to ensure delivery of Enhanced HRSN Services and subsequent referral closure

More details on each of these responsibilities can be found on the following pages of this section.

Figure 5-1: Member journey from Screening to Social Care Navigation, service provision, and referral closure

sections.title: Screening
sections.text:
b. SCREENING

i. HRSN Screening overview
Consistently identifying the unmet HRSNs of Medicaid members is the first step to addressing their HRSNs.

OHIP’s aim is that every Medicaid member receives an HRSN Screening annually, on a rolling 12-month basis,
and on an as-needed basis. Members will be screened using a standardized OHIP version of the AHC HRSN
Screening Tool or AHC Embedded Tool, to assess member HRSNs related to housing and utilities, nutrition,
transportation, employment, education, and interpersonal safety. Regularly screening members across these
domains will improve the identification of HRSNs and show how HRSNs are evolving over time.

There must be sufficient capacity in each region to conduct HRSN Screening for all Medicaid members and for
Screening results to be consistently acted on with timely follow-up. The following sections provide details on the
role of various stakeholders in HRSN Screening, Screening methodology, use of the standardized AHC HRSN
Screening Tool, and reimbursement for Screening.

ii. Who will conduct HRSN Screening
SCN Lead Entities will be responsible for ensuring there is sufficient capacity in their region(s) to conduct
Screenings of all Medicaid members. This includes building additional Screening capacity as needed.

SCN Lead Entities are expected to coordinate with partners in the regional ecosystem (e.g., HRSN service
providers, health care providers, independent practice associations (IPAs), care management providers, MCOs)
to ensure that they have sufficient collective capacity to screen all Medicaid members for HRSNs.

OHIP recognizes that many health and HRSN services providers already conduct HRSN Screenings and
encourages continued Screening by these organizations. These organizations are often uniquely positioned in
their role as trusted partners to local communities and the ability to reach the Medicaid population.
[[p.57]]
Screenings conducted using the OHIP-standardized tool by the SCN or other organizations can be used to
facilitate Social Care Navigation by the SCN.

MCOs are encouraged to conduct Screening but will not be reimbursed. Please see Section e. MCO Contract
Requirements with OHIP, Part iv. MCO Risk Adjustment.

iii. Handoffs to SCN for Screening
OHIP strongly encourages SCNs to work with other stakeholders in the ecosystem to coordinate handoffs of
Medicaid members for Screening by the SCN (for example, MCOs are encouraged to establish workflows for
MCO care managers to conduct “warm hand-offs” of members to SCN Social Care Navigators). OHIP will not
require a specific process for organizations that wish to conduct a handoff to the SCN for a member to be
screened. However, in order to facilitate handoffs, SCNs are expected to provide contact information (on an as-
requested basis and made publicly available on the SCN website) that external stakeholders can use to contact
the SCN to request that a member is screened and to share member contact information.

SCNs should make every effort to follow up with the member and conduct member Screening within five (5)
business days of receiving information about the member.

iv. Screening methodology
Screening modality and encounter: To ensure that all members can access Screening according to their needs
and preferences, SCNs should offer Screening in different modalities, at accessible times, and in culturally and
linguistically competent ways, in accordance with National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically
Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Health and Health Care.

SCN Lead Entities and entities conducting Screening within the Network will agree on the specific modalities,
times, languages, etc. in which Screening will be offered. It is the responsibility of the SCN Lead Entity to ensure
that the Network overall has sufficient Screening capacity and capabilities.

Screening involves asking a standard series of questions, coupled with the empathetic engagement with
individuals to understand their life context, specific needs, and HRSN service preferences. OHIP expects
Screeners to treat members with identified unmet HRSNs with care and empathy, including offering time to
discuss their needs and potential next steps (e.g., Eligibility Assessment, referral). (For more information on
Screening capacity and capabilities, see HRSN Network Capacity and Access).

Member consent for Screening data sharing: Entities conducting HRSN Screening are required to receive
informed consent from members to share their information and Screening information with the Social Care
Network (for additional information, see Member Consent). If a member declines to provide consent, the
Screening will not proceed.

Screening frequency: OHIP aims to ensure that each Medicaid member will receive a HRSN Screening annually
and as needed due to a self-reported major life event (see Table 5-1). A major life event may be identified by any
contracted entity within the SCN that is authorized to have direct contact with a member (e.g., through
Screening, Eligibility Assessment, or delivery of HRSN services).
[[p.58]]
SCNs conducting Screening will receive reimbursement for a member’s first annual Screening or upon a major
life event requiring re-screening. Additional Screenings conducted within a year from the initial Screening (in the
absence of a major life event) are NOT eligible for reimbursement.

Table 5-1: Frequency of HRSN Screening

    Reason for Screening      Details

    Annual Screening          Members will be eligible for reimbursed HRSN Screening annually (rolling 12
                              months).
    Major life event          Members will also be eligible for reimbursed HRSN Screening if a major life event
                              occurs. If the Screener identifies a major life event during their interaction with
                              the member, or if a member was referred to the SCN for a Screening as a result
                              of a major life event, the member may be re-screened within the same year and
                              the Screener may be reimbursed for the Re-screen.

                              A major life event is a permanent or fluctuating event in a member’s life that may
                              be identified by any contracted entity within the SCN that is authorized to have
                              direct contact with a member (e.g., through Screening, Eligibility Assessment,
                              HRSN service delivery, service follow-up).

                              Members will be eligible for their annual Screening 12 months after their original
                              Screening date, regardless of any Re-Screens due to a major life event.

                              Major life events may include:
                                 • Change in functioning (including an increase or decrease of symptoms or
                                      a new diagnosis);
                                 • Inpatient or outpatient hospital admittance and/or discharge;
                                 • Serious injury;
                                 • Admittance, discharge, or transfer from detox or residential placement;
                                 • Significant change in housing, including move to a different SCN region,
                                      move to different housing, or loss of housing;
                                 • Significant change in income or support resources;
                                 • Significant change to family, including but not limited to: marriage or
                                      divorce; giving birth (regardless of outcome) to or adopting a child, loss
                                      of a family member;
                                 • Arrest;
                                 • Loss of benefits; or
                                 • Change in coverage from FFS to Managed Care

Reimbursement for Screening: To receive reimbursement through the SCN program, Screening must:

•     Be conducted on behalf of a Medicaid member: While Screenings of individuals beyond Medicaid members
      may be sent to the SHIN-NY, only Screenings of eligible Medicaid members (both FFS and Managed Care
      members) will receive reimbursement
[[p.59]]
    Use the standardized tool: Screenings must use the AHC HRSN Screening Tool or AHC Embedded Tool. Refer
    to section e. Data sets, Terminologies and Coding for technical Screening requirements. Questions cannot be
    adjusted or changed. If a contracted screener would like support embedding the AHC screen, they may
    contact SDH@health.ny.gov for assistance.
•   Answer key AHC Screening questions: In order for a Screening to be reimbursed, AHC question 0 (consent)
    must be answered, and 1 additional AHC question within #1-12 must have a response corresponding to a
    valid LOINC code which cannot be a Data Absent Reason code. This applies to screens completed within the
    SCN IT platform or outside of the SCN IT Platform. Refer to section e. Data sets, Terminologies and Coding
    for Data Absent Reason coding requirements.

•   Be entered into the SCN IT Platform or a Platform that can share data with the SCN IT platform: While
    Screening by organizations that are not contracted as part of the SCN is encouraged, organizations must be
    contracted with the SCN Lead Entity in order to receive reimbursement. Screeners contracted with the SCN
    Lead Entity can either use the SCN IT Platform or an off-platform screening tool capable of sharing data with
    the SCN IT platform or QE
            o Screenings conducted within the SCN IT Platform: Screening can be conducted by employees of
                the SCN Lead Entity or by contracted organizations in the Network. Screening conducted within
                the Network will receive reimbursement (assuming criteria outlined in Reimbursement for
                Screening Section below are met). Refer to section e. Data sets, Terminologies and Coding for
                SCN IT Platform technical Screening requirements.
                ▪ Wherever possible, OHIP encourages SCN Social Care Navigators to conduct both Screening
                     and Eligibility Assessment in the same encounter to streamline member experience and
                     allow faster access to services.
           o Screenings conducted outside the SCN IT Platform: Contracted organizations using off-platform
                screening tools are encouraged to conduct Screenings and send the results to SHIN-NY via a QE.
                These Screens can then be shared with and acted on by the SCNs. Screenings conducted by
                organizations that are not contracted with the SCN Lead Entity will not be reimbursed, but SCN
                IT Platforms must be able to accept any/all Screenings routed for their members. Refer to
                section e. Data sets, Terminologies and Coding as well as “Data Specification for Providers
                Submitting Screenings via CSV or CCDA” linked on the NYeC website under “Data Specifications
                for Providers – View Data Specifications” for technical requirements of Screenings conducted
                outside the SCN IT Platform.
                ▪ OHIP encourages organizations conducting Screening to contract with their regional SCN
                     Lead Entity in order to receive reimbursement
                ▪ SCN Social Care Navigators are expected to conduct Social Care Navigation for members
                     who have an identified unmet HRSN in a timely manner (see HRSN Network Capacity and
                     Access)

•   Be the member’s annual Screen or a verified Re-Screen due to a major life event: SCNs will only be
    reimbursed for one Screen per year (rolling 12 months), or for a Re-Screen due to a major life event. Major
    life events can warrant paid Re-Screening and can be tracked using the Re-Screening HCPCS code and
    supporting modifier to indicate it is a valid Re-Screening. If a Medicaid Managed Care member undergoes
    an Eligibility Assessment following the Screening, the Social Care Navigator should document the life event
[[p.60]]
    in the Medicaid Managed Care member’s Social Care Plan (see Table 5-1 for list of major life events).
    Members can receive up to 1 reimbursed Re-Screen per year following their initial Annual Screening.

•   Involve 1:1 member interaction: Screening must include a 1:1 interaction between the screener and
    member for the screener to be eligible to receive payment. If a member independently completes
    Screening (e.g., via a paper form) and thereafter discusses the results with a provider, the provider may be
    reimbursed for the time spent engaging with the member on the Screening. Providers will not receive
    payment if a member self-screens without a subsequent 1:1 interaction with a provider, including
    Screenings in which the member only uses an online Self-Screening tool or other digital Screening with no
    1:1 human interaction (e.g., online form, AI chatbot)
           o Screening reimbursement is time based and includes the time spent explaining the SCN program
                to a member, obtaining consent, walking through the Screening, inputting the member’s
                information and answers to Screening questions, and responding to the member’s questions
                about next steps. If a Screening takes fewer than 8 minutes, it will not be reimbursed. If a
                Screening takes 8 minutes or more, it may be reimbursed.
           o If a Self-Screening is not accurate (e.g., expired CIN, incorrect date of birth, inaccurate
                responses) and requires SCN to reach out to the member to validate member identity and re-
                enter member Screening answers into the IT Platform, the 1:1 interaction with a member to
                update the Screening may be reimbursed.

Geographic location of Screening: Members can be screened anywhere in the state, regardless of their assigned
SCN region and SCNs are encouraged to contract with each other to facilitate reimbursement for Screening as
needed. If a member presents to a SCN that is not their current SCN (based on current address registered with
Medicaid, as reflected in MEVS), the SCN may screen the member or refer them to the currently assigned SCN.
The member’s currently assigned SCN should reimburse the SCN that conducted the Screening if contracted with
the SCN Lead Entity. If the member is screened outside of the currently assigned SCN region, the Screening will
be a part of the daily Screening extract (flat file) or real-time FHIR API that goes via the SHIN-NY to the currently
assigned SCN, not to the SCN that conducted the Screening (see Member relocation and change of address for
more details).

The current SCN (based on current Medicaid member address registered with LDSS or NYSOH) must hold a
record of the member’s Screenings in the IT Platform either by obtaining it from the SHIN-NY or re-screening the
member (moving regions is considered a major life event and therefore a valid reason for a Re-screening).

Checking for duplication of Screening: When Screening is conducted by Social Care Navigators within the SCN,
OHIP expects that the Social Care Navigator will confirm that the Screen is not duplicative of an existing Screen
on file for the member.

SCNs will incorporate Screenings from a daily extract or real-time FHIR API from the SHIN-NY into the SCN IT
Platform that Social Care Navigators will be able to query to determine Screening status and monitor for
duplication. Social Care Navigators must have the ability to query the member data from the SCN IT Platform.

The process to check for duplication of Screenings is similar to that used by ecosystem partners to submit
Screening for Social Drivers of Health measure as a reported Clinical Quality Measure (CQM). To prevent
duplication of HRSN Screening efforts, SCN Lead Entities will need to provide training and education to Social
[[p.61]]
Care Navigators in their contracted Network for steps to query SCN IT Platform to confirm if a Screening was
already completed within the past year.

Screening of children and youth: OHIP’s vision is for New York State to be a healthy community of thriving
individuals and families. To advance that vision, OHIP is deeply committed to SCNs strengthening the physical,
mental, and social well-being of New York’s children and youth. Children and youth participating in New York’s
SCN program will experience a similar member journey to adult participants: they should be screened for unmet
HRSNs, connected with appropriate HRSN services, receive services and Social Care Planning, and receive follow-
up to determine whether their HRSNs have been addressed and if ongoing services are needed.

However, there are a few details of the SCN program that will be somewhat different for children and youth,
particularly around Screening, assessment for SCN eligibility, and Social Care Planning. The primary aspects of
the program that are distinct for children and youth can be found in sections Screening (this section), Eligibility
Assessment, and Social Care Plans.

    •   Expectations for Screening minors: As with adult Medicaid members, SCNs are responsible for Screening
        all children and youth enrolled in Medicaid for unmet HRSNs using the same standardized AHC HRSN
        Screening tool, or AHC Embedded Tool. Screening should be done for each individual Medicaid member.
        SCNs are encouraged, but not required, to screen parents and caregivers and other children in the
        household enrolled in Medicaid at the same time as the children and youth they are screening.
    •   Role of the child vs. the parent, guardian, or legally authorized representative when screening children:
              o For children under 10 years old: The parent, guardian, or legally authorized representative will
                   respond to the Screening questions on the child’s behalf, and the parent, guardian, or legally
                   authorized representative can consent to have the child’s Screening information shared.
              o For children ages 10 and older: The parent, guardian, or legally authorized representative will
                   typically respond to the Screening questions on the child’s behalf, but the child can agree to be
                   screened and answer Screening questions on their own when necessary and the child is
                   developmentally able to understand (e.g., when adolescents present on their own for
                   confidential health care services). The child can consent to sharing Screening information.
              o Parent and Guardian: At the discretion of the SCN Lead Entity, Social Care Navigators may
                   request for a parent or guardian to identify themselves.
              o Legally Authorized Representative: At the discretion of the SCN Lead Entity, Social Care
                   Navigators may request documentation (court issued, etc.) from anyone presenting as a legally
                   authorized representative. The Social Care Navigator will save this documentation in the Social
                   Care Plan.
    •   Guidance for minors living independently or children in foster care: Minors living independently of
        parents or that are parents, pregnant, and/or married, and who are otherwise capable of completing
        the Screening on their own behalf can do so. Children in Voluntary Foster Care Agencies (VFCAs) may be
        screened by the Foster Care Agency and have the guardian or parent complete the Screening on the
        minor’s behalf.
    •   Training requirements to screen children and youth:
             o OHIP does not require a child-specific training for HRSN Screeners. However, all Screeners are
                  expected to complete the list of trainings suggested in the Training Expectations section,
                  including trauma-informed training
[[p.62]]
            o     SCN organizations working with children and youth are expected to understand their legal
                  obligations relating to minors. SCNs are encouraged to use and leverage external resources as
                  they are available (e.g., NYCLU Guide to Minors’ Rights in NYS) to understand the rights of
                  children and minors and operate within legal requirements
    •   Screening documentation for children: As for adults, all Screening responses are required to be entered
        into the SCN IT Platform (either directly or through a platform capable of sharing data with the SCN IT
        platform). Platforms are not required to capture a data element for the name / relationship of the
        person who completed the Screening on a child's behalf. However, SCNs are expected to include this in
        the Social Care Plan
    •   Flexibility to tailor Screening processes for children: When conducting Screening for children and youth,
        SCNs are encouraged to consider tailoring their Screening processes where appropriate, such as where
        the Screening takes place and how questions are explained

v. AHC HRSN Screening Tool
Members will be screened using the required AHC HRSN Screening Tool, or AHC Embedded Tool, to assess needs
across a range of HRSN domains. These Screenings will contain questions related to six HRSN domains: housing
and utilities, nutrition, transportation, employment, education, and interpersonal safety. Screenings will help
identify unmet HRSNs and tailor services to address those needs.

A sample of the tool is shared below and made available by CMS.

The AHC HRSN Screening Tool is distinct from the UAS Uniform Assessment System (UAS) Community Health
Assessment, and SCN Screening efforts are separate from the UAS requirements.

The AHC Embedded Tools must contain identical wording and LOINC coding to the AHC HRSN Screening Tool for
all question-and-answer pairs, including “Question 0” in order to obtain necessary consent. AHC questions
cannot be adjusted or changed. If non-AHC questions and answers are included in AHC Embedded tools, they
will not be used to inform member outreach.

If a contracted screening entity would like technical assistance verifying the accuracy of their AHC Embedded
Tool, they may contact SDH@health.ny.gov for support. Screeners will use the AHC HRSN Screening Tool or a
comparable assessment instrument with identical LOINC coding as the AHC Tool for question-and-answer pairs
and must be approved by OHIP. It must also contain “Question 0” to obtain necessary consent. Questions
cannot be adjusted or changed.

SCNs should reach out to OHIP Contract Managers to speak with NYHER data subject matter experts before
conducting any proposed mappings to the LOINC coding in the AHC Tool.

Each answer to Screening questions has a corresponding LOINC code that is used to determine if the Screening is
positive (for an overview of these LOINC Codes, see Screening for Social Risks: LOINC Codes). The following table
outlines permitted response option to each Screening question.

Table 5-2: AHC HRSN Screening Tool

      work or a job?                         •   Yes, help keeping work

      high school diploma, GED or

 might not be safe.
 9.   How often does anyone, including       •   Never (1)
      family and friends, physically hurt    •   Rarely (2)
      you?                                   •   Sometimes (3)

      family and friends, insult or talk     •   Rarely (2)
      down to you?                           •   Sometimes (3)
                                             •   Fairly often (4)

                                             •   Not asked
 11. How often does anyone, including        •   Never (1)
      family and friends, threaten you       •   Rarely (2)
      with harm?                             •   Sometimes (3)

      family and friends, scream or curse    •   Rarely (2)

AHC Screening Questions #1-8: In line with the established AHC HRSN Screening tool and in order to ensure high
quality Screening data, “Asked but declined” and “Not asked” should NOT be included as response options for
questions #1-8.
[[p.65]]
AHC Screening Questions #9-12: Given the sensitive nature of questions #9-12 (Interpersonal Safety), they may
not always be asked and members may not always answer. “Asked but declined” and “Not asked” are permitted
responses. They should be available in the IT platform and Screeners may use them as appropriate.

If needed, Screeners can still proceed through the Screening even if they need to leave any of questions #1-12
blank with an appropriate Data Absent Reason code. Refer to section e. Data sets, Terminologies, and Coding for
Data Absent Reason coding requirements. These Screenings should still be actioned if an unmet need is
indicated for other Screening questions (i.e., initiating Eligibility Assessment for identified unmet need).

vi. Considerations for interpersonal safety questions asked during Screening
Creating a safe and appropriate environment for Screening: The interpersonal safety (IPS) questions should
only be asked in a safe and appropriate environment. Based on their training, Social Care Navigators should
determine when it is appropriate not to ask these questions (for example, if a partner or family member is with
the member while they are being screened).

Providing support to members: While a member may receive an interpersonal safety score below the threshold
needed to identify the member as having an unmet HRSN regarding safety (e.g., due to member not answering
all 4 interpersonal safety questions), the member may still benefit from support related to interpersonal safety.
When appropriate, Social Care Navigators can offer navigating a member to existing local, state, or federal
resources for interpersonal safety support, even if their safety score is not above the threshold. If a member has
interpersonal safety concerns as confirmed during the eligibility assessment and wants assistance, the Social
Care Navigator must prioritize issuing the referral to existing local, state or federal services as close to same day
of the eligibility assessment as possible.

It is OHIP’s goal that SCN Lead Entities establish HRSN Screening processes that appropriately support and
ensure the safety of children and youth. OHIP expects that SCN Lead Entities will ensure Social Care Navigators
undertake appropriate training so they can support members and address member needs, including those
related to IPS. In addition to requiring Social Care Navigators to take the NYS Mandated Reporter training, OHIP
encourages SCN Lead Entities to share guidance with Social Care Navigators and HRSN service providers in their
Network on working effectively with children and youth.

Screeners and Social Care Navigators should familiarize themselves with resources available for members in
their community. Many communities have emergency personnel, including advocates and law enforcement,
who are specially trained to respond to intimate violence crises. The NYS Office for the Prevention of Domestic
Violence provides many resources including, but not limited to, a 24/7 hotline (1-800-942-6906), text line (1-
844-997-2121), and web chat for confidential support.

IPS questions and eligibility for services: Answers to IPS questions asked during the HRSN Screening do not
impact a member’s eligibility to receive services. Following the member’s Screening, a Social Care Navigator will
assess a member’s eligibility to receive Enhanced HRSN Services during the Eligibility Assessment. Refer to Table
5-16: Eligibility determination pathways for each Enhanced Population and Enhanced HRSN Service for guidance
on how to verify the criteria of “a health condition, including behavioral health and developmental syndromes,
stemming from trauma, child abuse, and neglect.” Answers to IPS questions in the HRSN Screening do not verify
this eligibility criteria.

sections.title: Social Care Navigation
sections.text:
c. SOCIAL CARE NAVIGATION

i. Social Care Navigators
Systematically addressing the HRSNs of Medicaid members requires that Screening be the beginning of a
process through which the right HRSN services are identified, the member is connected with HRSN service
providers in their community, and there is follow up to ensure services were delivered and the member’s needs
have been addressed.

Social Care Navigators are essential to enabling that end-to-end process, delivering a seamless experience to
members from Screening to delivery of services. They are accountable for ensuring that members get the HRSN
services they need in way that is accessible and appropriately tailored to each member’s needs. Members can
also use the SCN’s Social Care Navigators as their direct point of contact for ongoing HRSNs.

Social Care Navigators may be employed by the SCN Lead Entity or by other entities in the Network (such as
HRSN service providers and health care providers) or MCOs. For example, care managers or resource
coordinators employed by MCOs, health care providers, or care management providers may play Social Care
Navigator roles as long as they are contracted by the SCN Lead Entity to perform the role and are trained to use
the SCN IT Platform. While MCOs may play Social Care Navigator roles to screen, navigate, and refer members,
they will not receive payment for doing so.

Although New York State does not require it, OHIP envisions that Social Care Navigators will be Community
Health Workers. Social Care Navigators serve as trusted community members who have the ability to broadly
support health and well-being.

ii. Reimbursement for Social Care Navigation
Social Care Navigation will be reimbursed via payment based on the HRSN fee schedule for care management
(for 15-minute increments). Attempts by a Social Care Navigator to contact a member (e.g., if a member cannot
be reached after a Screening that identifies an unmet HRSN) will not be reimbursed. Social Care Navigation must
be conducted using the SCN IT Platform to be eligible for reimbursement.

In order to receive reimbursement through the SCN Program, Navigation must:
    • Be conducted on behalf of a Medicaid member: Only Navigation of enrolled Medicaid members (both
        FFS and Managed Care members) will receive reimbursement. See Covered HRSN Service, Section 1.
        Care Management part 1.1 Navigation Services (Eligibility Assessment and Navigation) for FFS and non-
        eligible Medicaid Managed Care members and part 1.2a Enhanced HRSN Care Management (Eligibility
        Assessment) for eligible Medicaid Managed Care members
    • Be conducted by a Social Care Navigator: Service must be delivered by Social Care Navigator; Social Care
        Navigators may include employees of the SCN Lead Entity or of organizations that are contracted as part
        of the Network. Navigation will not be reimbursed if conducted through an automated program or
        website
    • Be time spent engaging with the member or on behalf of the member: Social Care Navigators will only be
        reimbursed for time spent with a live person (on the phone, in person, virtual) engaging with a member
[[p.67]]
        or other stakeholders (e.g., parent, guardian, legally authorized representative, clinical provider) on
        behalf of the member with regards to eligibility or care coordination
    •   Be conducted using the SCN IT Platform or system that is able to send referral information to the SCN IT
        Platform: The Social Care Navigator must send the referral information either through the SCN IT
        platform or through an integrated or interoperable application that is able to incorporate referral
        information into the SCN IT platform. For example, if a provider has a different IT system from the SCN
        but has an EHR module from that system and is able to send referral data to the SCN’s platform or the
        SCN platform is able to receive data via FHIR integration, Navigation can be reimbursed
    •   Be documented in the Social Care Plan: Details of Navigation to Enhanced HRSN Services, including any
        questions asked during the assessment, must be documented in the member’s Social Care Plan

iii. Navigation Process
The Navigation process includes validating member eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services, managing Closed
Loop Referrals for HRSN Services, and developing Social Care Plans for eligible Medicaid Managed Care
members.

Eligibility Assessment. This includes Social Care Navigators working with the member to confirm their unmet
HRSNs by selecting granular ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT descriptions; understanding the current services a member
may already be receiving; and discussing additional Social Risk Factors and clinical criteria to understand which
HRSN Enhanced Services a member may be eligible for. This assessment will be based on information provided
in the Enhanced Services Member File shared by the MCO and additional information provided by the member
and/or their health care provider.

Navigation to existing federal, state, or local services or referral to HRSN services. Depending on the outcome
of their Eligibility Assessment, members may be referred to HRSN Enhanced services, or to existing state,
federal, and local benefit programs. Navigation to existing services includes connection to Medicaid clinical care
management programs, such as Health Homes. The Enhanced Population will be navigated under HRSN Care
Management. Social Care Navigators are responsible for changing statuses to “Completed” after a member
accepts navigation to local, state, or federal services.

Social Care Plans. Social Care Navigators will be responsible for developing Social Care Plans for eligible
members that include a summary of member needs, eligibility, and services to which members are referred.

sections.title: Eligibility Assessment
sections.text:
d. ELIGIBILITY ASSESSMENT

i. Medicaid Member Eligibility
New York State has worked with CMS to determine which HRSN services can be reimbursed for specific
populations through NYHER. Medicaid members whose Screenings demonstrate unmet HRSNs should receive an
Eligibility Assessment to determine eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services.

Eligible Medicaid Managed Care members who meet certain criteria (determined by the Eligibility Assessment)
may receive Enhanced HRSN Services. Other Medicaid members may be directed to existing federal, state, and
local programs, including members who are also receiving Enhanced HRSN Services, when applicable. A
member’s eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services does not impact or change general Medicaid eligibility in New
York State or their enrollment with their MCO.

Certain populations are excluded from receiving Screening, Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN Services that are
reimbursed through NYHER. NYHER cannot fund Screening, Navigation, or Enhanced HRSN Services for the
following populations listed in Table 5-3. Members in these excluded populations have been identified and
excluded upstream of the SCNs in the Medicaid Eligibility File (MEF) by OHIP and the Enhanced Services Member
File (ESMF) by MCOs. Members who move from an eligible population to an excluded population can be
identified in the Disenrollment Change Report (DCR) with “HRSN” as the reason they dropped off the MEF.

For more detailed information and examples for determining member eligibility and utilizing the MEF, ESMF,
DCR, and MEVS, please refer to the Data and Systems Implementation Guidance (DSIG).

Eligibility timeframe: Enhanced HRSN Services will be delivered by the SCN for a pre-determined duration
period. Most Enhanced HRSN Services will be delivered for up to 6 months and may be used in increments.
Selected services may be renewed for an additional 6 months (3.2a Medically Tailored Meals; 3.2b Clinically
Appropriate Home Delivered Meals; 3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions; 3.4
Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable Groceries). Other services may be renewed in 6-month increments up to the
duration of the waiver (2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services; 3.1 Nutrition Counseling and Education;
4.1 HRSN Transportation). Additional details are available in the fee schedule. Some members may be eligible to
receive services for longer periods (e.g., pregnant individuals may receive Nutrition services for a longer period
of time) (see Covered HRSN Services). Social Care Navigators may consider the member’s upcoming renewal or
end date in making determinations related to Enhanced HRSN Service delivery. For recurring services (e.g.,
services that require more than a one-time delivery), the Social Care Navigator MAY (at the discretion of the
SCN) refer the member for Enhanced HRSN service delivery only up until the renewal date or end date,
whichever comes first. SCNs will need to establish workflows for Social Care Navigators to re-authorize services
as appropriate based on member renewal and reenrollment.

Lookback period to determine eligibility: When a lookback period is needed to determine population eligibility
(e.g., Medicaid High Utilizer, etc.), MCOs and SCN Lead Entities will use a 12-month rolling look back period, not
the calendar year.

Duration of eligibility: It is important for SCNs to ensure that only eligible Medicaid members receive Enhanced
HRSN Services. Members remain eligible to have services, for which they are eligible to receive, initiated for up
to 6 months following the Eligibility Assessment. During this 6-month period, members can be referred to
services without requiring a new Eligibility Assessment. However, before making a referral, Social Care
Navigators must still verify the member’s Medicaid eligibility in MEVS on the day of the referral. If the member
has not started services for which they are eligible within 6 months of receiving an Eligibility Assessment,
members seeking to start Enhanced HRSN Services must undergo a new Eligibility Assessment.

If members have initiated services within 6 months of their Eligibility Assessment, they do NOT need to receive
another Eligibility Assessment at 6 months. Instead, members should exhaust the duration of services for which
they were authorized and receive an additional Eligibility Assessment only if services require renewal.

Reassessment of eligibility: If a member is determined to be ineligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, a re-
assessment will only be reimbursed after 12 months of their initial Eligibility Assessment, unless they experience
a major life event.

Service duration: The 6-month service duration for Enhanced HRSN Services and for 6-month re-authorization is
defined as 6 calendar months from the Service Start Date (e.g., service start date of 8/1/25 and service end date
of 1/31/26). Service Start Date must be calculated from the 1st date of service provision for the member where
applicable (e.g., 6 months of MTM is based on date of 1st meal provision to the member).
[[p.73]]
Service duration pause: A member may decide to pause their Enhanced HRSN Service provision for various
reasons and should communicate planned and unplanned breaks in service to their Social Care Navigator and
HRSN service provider. A member’s request for a pause in service will not impact the length of their approved
service duration.

 o If member will be in an institutional/residential facility for more than 90 days and does not have a
