Member’s SCN: A Medicaid member’s SCN is based on their latest residential address by county (not zip code)
assigned by Medicaid. Members must receive services in the SCN covering the county of their current residential
address (based on Medicaid data). If a member moves out of one SCN service area and into another, the
outgoing SCN will communicate member address updates to the MCOs and work with members to update their
address with Local Department of Social Services (LDSS) or New York State of Health (NYSOH). Outgoing SCN will
coordinate and hand-off of the member to the new SCN (see Member relocation section).

ii. Eligibility Assessment process
Once a member is screened and found to have an unmet HRSN, a Social Care Navigator will obtain member
consent to conduct an Eligibility Assessment and verbal attestation that information provided during the
Eligibility Assessment is complete and accurate to the best of the member’s knowledge.

The Social Care Navigator will then verify the member’s identity and Medicaid eligibility. Social Care Navigators
must confirm member’s eligibility to receive Navigation reimbursed via NYHER (see Table 5-3 for excluded
populations). Eligibility determination requires the coordinated use of multiple data sources that provide
complementary information on members. While MEVS / ePACES serves as the source of truth for real-time
Medicaid eligibility, the MEF, ESMF, and DCR provide supplemental and historical context that
support accurate determination. Once confirmed, a Social Care Navigator will assess the member’s eligibility to
receive Enhanced HRSN Services using the ESMF, and Tables 5-13, 5-14, 5-15 and 5-16 as support. For a high-
level overview of the steps of this Assessment, see Figure 5-2. A list of standardized questions built in the SCN IT
Platform will facilitate the Assessment. If needed, the Social Care Navigator can also ask additional questions to
better understand the member’s needs.
[[p.74]]
Figure 5-2: Eligibility Assessment activities

Eligibility Assessment requirements differ by population:

    •   For FFS members: Only steps 1-4 and step 6 are required

    •   For MMC members who are part of an Enhanced Population: Steps 1-9 are required

    •   For MMC members who are NOT part of an Enhanced Population: Only steps 1-6 are required

Eligibility Assessment steps

Step 1. Collect member consent and attestation to complete and accurate information. Member consent must
be documented in the SCN IT Platform

    •   The Social Care Navigator must ask for the member's consent to conduct the Eligibility Assessment using
        the following language:
        I would like to see, based on your medical history including information Medicaid collects, if you qualify
        for any services that could be helpful and which would be free to you. Is this okay with you? Do you have
        any questions?
    •   The Social Care Navigator must ask for the member’s verbal attestation that information provided
        during the Eligibility Assessment will be complete and accurate to the best of the member’s knowledge

Step 2. Confirm the member’s identity and their Medicaid enrollment

The Social Care Navigator should utilize (Medicaid Eligibility Verification System (MEVS) or ePACES as a source of
truth to verify the member eligibility and their Medicaid enrollment status in FFS or MMC as an eligible
[[p.75]]
population to receive services reimbursed via NYHER. See Table 5-3 for excluded populations. This step is used
to confirm that the member is actively enrolled in Medicaid at the time of service. Members in excluded
populations, see Table 5-3, have been identified and removed upstream of the SCNs through the Medicaid
Eligibility File (MEF) by OHIP and the Enhanced Services Member File (ESMF) by MCOs. Members who transition
from an eligible population to an excluded population can be identified in the Disenrollment Change Report
(DCR), which will show “HRSN” as the disenrollment reason. Additionally, most codes to identify excluded
populations are available in the MEVS and ePACES responses. SCNs can contact a member's MCO to determine
excluded population status if unavailable in MEVS / ePACES.

SCN IT Platform vendors are required to have permanent integration with MEVS within the SCN IT Platform. If
the Social Care Navigator is unable to access MEVS through SCN IT Platform, then the Social Care Navigator may
submit a request for eligibility verification by:

    1. Checking ePACES and reviewing the enrollment details OR
    2. Calling eMedNY’s telephone verification service to confirm enrollment. See additional guidance for
       ePACES/eMedNY methods here

If Social Care Navigators do not have access to eMedNY or ePACES, SCN LEs may establish a workflow whereby
LEs can check these sources and provide information to Social Care Navigators.

If Social Care Navigators are using ePACES or eMedNY’s telephone verification services to confirm MMC
enrollment, Social Care Navigators should see Table 5-3 above to understand if a member is part of a NYHER-
excluded population and therefore is not eligible for Screening, Navigation, or Enhanced HRSN Services.

Situations in which member’s address does not match MEVS/ePACES: At the time of Eligibility Assessment,
Social Care Navigators should confirm member ID and residential address, collected verbally, before performing
Navigation services. If member indicates their address is different from the address listed in MEVS / ePACES, the
Social Care Navigator should use the address provided by the member as the primary address for Enhanced
HRSN Services.

If a member reports a different residential address within the same SCN region: Social Care Navigators should
document member’s new address in Social Care Plan and initiate the process to update the member’s address
(see Member relocation and change of address for more details).

If member reports a different residential address in a different SCN region: Social Care Navigators should
initiate the process to update the member’s address (see member relocation and change of address for more
details).

•   Social Care Navigator should note member’s new address in Social Care Plan and initiate communication
    with the SCN Lead Entity associated with where the member currently lives, to facilitate a handoff within 5
    business days to enable new SCN Lead Entity to navigate the member
•   New SCN Lead Entity associated with member’s new address will need to wait until member address is
    updated in NYSOH or LDSS and member appears in MEVS / ePACES, MEF or ESMF to conduct Eligibility
    Assessment. Member may still be navigated to existing federal, state, and local services in the meantime

Demographic and Physical Disability questions: In most cases, the set of Demographic and Physical Disability
questions will have been answered during the member’s HRSN Screening. However, if a member did not
[[p.76]]
previously answer the Demographic and Physical Disability questions (either due to skipping or the Screening
taking place outside of the SCN IT Platform), they should be answered during the Eligibility Assessment.

The Social Care Navigator should engage with the member to gather their responses on the set of Demographic
and Physical Disability questions built into the SCN IT Platform (based on OHIP’s Minimum Viable Dataset).

See Screening section above for information on specific questions.

Step 3. Confirm understanding of the member’s HRSNs

Check the SCN IT Platform for the member’s HRSN Screening results and review any unmet needs with the
member. Social Care Navigators will then be required to select the appropriate granular ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT
assessment code(s) from a filtered set of code descriptions per the Social Care Coding document that captures
the specific unmet need from the member’s identified positive response(s) from screening. Entry of this code
serves to reinforce the screening answer(s) and constitutes a complete Eligibility Assessment. Identified unmet
HRSNs will be automatically mapped to ICD-10 Z codes and SNOMED-CT assessment codes by the SCN IT
Platform (see Eligibility Assessment Coding).

Situations in which a member’s needs identified during the Eligibility Assessment are different than the initial
Screening: If a member’s unmet HRSNs identified during Screening are different than those identified during the

                   • Capture via a SNOMED change or initiate a re-screening for the member: SNOMED
                       Requirements: The SNOMED CT or ICD 10 code associated with the need identified
                       during the initial Screen must be noted by the Social Care Navigator during the Eligibility
                       Assessment and captured in an observation assessment to send as a FHIR bundle.
                       Additionally, this observation assessment should include the SNOMED of “Not
[[p.77]]

                              428263003).

Step 4. Confirm that the member wants to receive help with unmet HRSNs

Ask if the member would like to receive services for unmet HRSNs. If they do not, end the assessment here.

Step 5. Check whether the member is included in an Enhanced Population

Use information in the Enhanced Services Member File (see Enhanced Services Member File) and from
interacting with the member to determine whether the member is part of an Enhanced Population for the SCN
program, meaning that they may be eligible to receive certain Enhanced HRSN Services.

As part of this process, the Social Care Navigator should ensure that the member they are assessing matches the
member listed in the Enhanced Services Member File using the “Member Identifier” fields. The Social Care
Navigator must also inform the member that information shared during the Eligibility Assessment could be
shared with the member’s MCO and with providers.

There are instances in which the information from the interaction between the Social Care Navigator and the
member supersedes information found in the Enhanced Services Member File (e.g., if relevant criteria are those
to which providers and/or members may attest). For more information see Criteria documentation and
attestation.

In the event the Social Care Navigator learns of information not included in the ESMF, the Social Care Navigator
should document any relevant additional information about the member in the SCN IT Platform and share with
the MCO through a process determined jointly by the MCO and SCN. If a member states they do not have, or do
not want to disclose, a specific clinical condition that the Enhanced Services Member File indicates the member
has, the Social Care Navigator will honor the member’s statement. The Social Care Navigator should not request
that the MCO remove information from the Member File. Members always have the option to decline services.

Step 6. Ask member follow-up questions within the Eligibility Assessment to better understand their unmet
HRSNs

Follow-up questions must be built into SCN IT Platform’s Eligibility Assessment. The member’s corresponding
answers must be documented in the member’s Social Care Plan or in the member’s profile. The questions are
intended for the Social Care Navigator and HRSN service providers that receive referrals to better understand
the nature of the member’s HRSNs and which services are most appropriate.

Through these questions, the Social Care Navigator will first identify if there is an opportunity to enroll the
member in federally funded benefits for relevant services such as SNAP, WIC, or TANF, then select the relevant
granular ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT descriptions of the member’s unmet needs, and lastly navigate the member
using the appropriate “Completed” status. If the member is currently receiving federal benefits, the Social Care
Navigator should identify what additional services are being provided to the member to avoid any potential
duplication of services.

For MMC members in an Enhanced Population, the following questions are required to be asked of members
based on HRSNs. All relevant questions should be answered with Yes / No as part of a comprehensive Eligibility
Assessment. The Social Care Navigator should only ask general questions and questions related to the member's
unmet HRSN domain(s). It is acceptable if the member declines or does not know the answer to these questions
within the Eligibility Assessment.

    i. General Follow-up Questions
    1. Is the member enrolled in TANF (OTDA)? If the member is enrolled in Managed Care and eligible for
       TANF, the Social Care Navigator can assist with a TANF application. The Social Care Navigator must select
       the appropriate ICD-10/ SNOMED-CT description and “Completed” status for navigation.
    2. What is the member’s current employment status?
    3. Does the member have income from any source?
[[p.80]]
    4. How many people are in the member’s household?

    ii.   Housing Follow-up Questions (only required if member has an unmet housing need)
    1.    What type of housing assistance does the member need?
    2.    Is their household currently working with a housing provider?
    3.    Is the member on any housing waitlists (i.e., HUD. Section 8, local housing authority, or other voucher
          programs) or receive a rental subsidy?

    iii. HRSN Transportation Follow-up Questions(only required if member has an unmet HRSN transportation
         need)
     1. What type of HRSN transportation assistance does the member need?
     2. For what activities does the member need help with HRSN transportation?
     3. Does the member already receive any transportation services?

    iv. Nutrition Follow-up Questions(only required if member has an unmet nutrition need)
    1. Is the member enrolled in SNAP (OTDA) and WIC? If the member is enrolled in Managed Care and
        eligible for SNAP or WIC, the Social Care Navigator can assist with an application. The Social Care
        Navigator must use the appropriate ICD-10/SNOMED-CT descriptions and “Completed” status for
        navigation.
    2. Is the member receiving any home-delivered meals or food services?
    3. Is the member currently receiving nutritional counseling or education?
    4. How many people in the member’s household need food assistance?
    5. Does the member have the ability to store food, such as a refrigerator?
    6. Does the member have cooking supplies such as pots, pans, utensils, plates, etc.?
    7. Does the member have any dietary restrictions or food allergies?

    v. Nutrition Decision Tree

For MMC members in an Enhanced Population, required questions for Nutrition Enhanced HRSN Services:
When navigating members to Enhanced HRSN Services, Social Care Navigators should determine the type of
Nutrition services that are appropriate for each member based on their unique needs and eligibility criteria.

During the Eligibility Assessment, for members who are eligible for BOTH prepared meals (3.2a Medically
Tailored Meals or 3.2b Clinically Appropriate Home Delivered Meals) and food prescriptions or pantry stocking
(3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions or 3.4 Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable
Groceries), Social Care Navigators are required to ask all members of a household the following questions to
determine the most appropriate service for each member.

Note, each member of the household may not require the same Nutrition service intensity (e.g., one member
may require Medically Tailored Meals, while another may be sufficiently served by Pantry Stocking). In addition,
individuals who live in the household of an eligible member should only be referred to Pantry Stocking or Food
Prescriptions, NOT Medically Tailored Meals. Exceptions must be approved by the SCN LE.
[[p.81]]
1. Can you prepare and serve adequate meals either by yourself or with the help of a caregiver?
   • If member answers “No” – Refer to MTM or Clinically appropriate meals (based on eligibility criteria)
   • If member answers “Yes” – Continue to question 2

2. Would you or a caregiver be able to prepare and serve adequate, nutritious meals if supplied
   with ingredients and instructions?
• If member answers “No” – Refer to MTM or Clinically appropriate meals (based on eligibility criteria)
• If member answers “Yes” – Refer to food prescription, food vouchers, or pantry stocking (based on eligibility
   criteria)

    vi. Asthma Remediation Decision Tree
For MMC members in an Enhanced Population with uncontrolled asthma, required questions and steps for
Housing Enhanced HRSN Services: When navigating members to Enhanced HRSN Services, Social Care
Navigators must determine the type of Housing Services that are appropriate for each member based on their
unique needs, ESMF indicator of uncontrolled asthma, and other eligibility criteria. Please note these questions
are for discussion purposes only with the member and are not SCN IT Platform requirements.

During the Eligibility Assessment, for members who have an unmet housing need and uncontrolled asthma,
Social Care Navigators are required to ask the following questions to determine the most appropriate service for
the member.

Step 1. Did the member screen positive for an unmet need in any of the three Housing and Utilities Screening
questions?

    •   If "Yes" – Member has a positive screen in the Housing and Utilities domain. Continue to Question 2 to
        assess eligibility for Asthma Remediation Services.
        Important Note: A Member/caregiver may reference other environmental triggers in the home
        impacting asthma that are not specifically listed under AHC HRSN Screening Tool, Question 2 (e.g.
        musty/mildewy carpet; indoor air quality issues like second-hand smoke, high humidity,
        uncomfortably high temperatures, cooking fumes in kitchen, pests such as cockroaches or rats,
        mildew, leaky pipes/plumbing or water stains from roof or windows, etc.). If these types of issues
        are noted, the appropriate Member response to AHC HRSN Screening Tool Question 1 (What is
        your living situation today?) should be “I have a place to live today, but I am worried about
        losing it in the future” because unhealthy housing conditions negatively impacting asthma
        may result in future housing instability. If newly identified housing needs are mentioned, proceed to
        rescreening steps outlined in Manual.

    •   If "No" – Member does not have a positive screen in the housing domain that would trigger Asthma
        Remediation; explore other domains as appropriate.

Step 2. Does the member self-identify as having uncontrolled asthma* or have an uncontrolled
asthma flag in the ESMF file?
[[p.82]]
    •   If ESMF files says "Yes" for uncontrolled asthma– see Step 3 Refer to Asthma Remediation Services
    •   If "Yes" via self-identification without presence of ESMF indicator for uncontrolled asthma – Provider
        Attestation must be completed prior to service referral (See Operations Manual Section 5v. Criteria for
        documentation and attestation). Once obtained, see Step 3 Refer to Asthma Remediation Services

        Note: In addition to 2.3 Asthma Remediation services (i.e., asthma trigger remediation, asthma self-
        management education support), members with uncontrolled asthma are automatically eligible for 2.2a
        Home Remediation Services when home conditions contribute to or worsen symptoms.

    •   If "No" via self-identification AND there is no ESMF indicator for Uncontrolled Asthma – Member is not
        eligible for Asthma Remediation Enhanced

Step 3. Refer to Asthma Remediation Services.

        Based on the member's reported home conditions and/or presence of an ESMF indicator for
        uncontrolled asthma, there is a potential need for asthma remediation services and/or home
        remediation services that could help improve the health of the member's home.

        Proceed with referral to 2.3 services per the Manual which includes 2.3a. Asthma Self-Management
        Education (ASME) and 2.3b. Dwelling Assessment and SOW Development. Refer to Operations Manual
        Table 5-25 for examples of eligible services and products.

        Note: Members eligible for Asthma Remediation are automatically eligible for 2.2a and b. Home
        Remediation Services (Mold & Pest and Ventilation) without an additional Attestation.

        If member declines 2.3b (dwelling assessment and SOW development) or if the landlord does not
        consent to a SOW with invasive measures, proceed with the full scope of 2.3a (ASME) which includes
        initial ASME visit, final ASME visit, Enhanced Care Management, provision of non-invasive products and
        services, and provision of additional asthma self-management education to the member between visits
        if needed.

Additional questions as needed: SCN Lead Entities and their IT Platforms may also add additional questions as
desired to support more effective and comprehensive referrals, such as questions about income level,
scheduling needs, delivery instructions, or the member’s existing care management. For example, members who
indicate that they are currently receiving care management (such as from an MCO or Health Home) the Social
Care Navigator can opt to collect the care manager’s contact information from the member and coordinate
HRSN service delivery with an existing care manager.

Follow-up questions for FFS and MMC non-enhanced population (not eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services)

A subset of assessment questions is required in the IT Platform EA for Social Care Navigators to ask FFS and non-
enhanced members in order to direct them to existing state, federal, and local resources that are appropriate
based on their need.
[[p.83]]
Figure 5-3: Follow-up questions to understand a member’s unmet needs

Step 7. Confirm the member’s eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services, including confirming Social Risk Factors
and ensuring there is no service duplication

Using information from the member interaction as well as the Enhanced Services Member File and the
Operations Manual, the Social Care Navigator needs to confirm that the member is eligible for one or more
Enhanced HRSN Services and is not already receiving duplicative services. Members do not need to be asked to
confirm information that is already marked with a “Y” on the ESMF file.

The Social Care Navigator should check that the member meets Social Risk Factors and clinical criteria (for
additional details, see HRSN Services). Only criteria pertaining to relevant Enhanced HRSN Services should be
checked.

Members must meet the Social Risk Factors related to their unmet need in Table 5-14 Social Risk Factors. This
step can be part of the overall eligibility check, but the member meeting the Social Risk Factor must be
documented either within the Eligibility Assessment or within the Social Care Plan.

Some Social Risk Factors, such as meeting the HUD definition of homelessness, require additional information
from the member to confirm the Social Risk Factor.

    a. Homeless verification (part of Medical Respite, Rent / Temporary Housing, Utility Setup / Assistance,
       Pre-Tenancy/Tenancy Supports, Community Transitional Supports, Housing Transition and Navigation):
       The Social Care Navigator will ensure that the member meets the HUD definition of homeless or at-risk
       of homelessness. See Table 5-16 for the documentation requirements. The Social Care Navigator will
       document the member’s current housing status and social risk eligibility within the IT Platform workflow
[[p.84]]
        of the Eligibility Assessment and upload documentation (if applicable). If this feature is not available yet
        in the platform, the Social Care Navigator should document the social risk criteria in the Social Care Plan.

After confirming eligibility (including Social Risk Factors), the Social Care Navigator should check for service
duplication. This should include reviewing Screening data to understand what benefits or services the member is
currently receiving, reviewing the Enhanced Services Member File for existing services being received, and
confirming the receipt and nature of services with the member to assess whether there is duplication.

A related federal or state benefit is not necessarily a duplication of services with an Enhanced HRSN Service. For
example, enrollment in a federal benefit such as SNAP or WIC is not considered duplicative of receiving 3.2
Medically Tailored Meals or Clinically Appropriate Home Delivered Meals, 3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally
Appropriate Food Prescriptions, and 3.4 Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable Groceries even though each involves
food. SNAP and WIC are designed to mitigate food insecurity for a household, whereas services 3.2 Medically
Tailored Meals or Clinically Appropriate Home Delivered Meals and 3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally
Appropriate Food Prescriptions must be approved by an RDN/CDN and are designed to improve health
outcomes and 3.4 Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable Groceries is designed to supplement weekly food for high-
risk children under 18 and pregnant / postpartum persons with identified food insecurity. Social Care Navigators
can assist members with applications to SNAP and WIC and/or other state programs involving food.

Healthy Homes Pilot Considerations:
    ●   A “Y” indicator for the Healthy Homes field on the ESMF flags to the Social Care Navigator that the
        member’s household consented to participate in the pilot and completed at least an initial asthma
        and/or dwelling visit under the Healthy Homes Pilot. Further discussion with the member is required to
        understand the extent of Pilot home improvement services delivered to the household and to
        determine whether additional supports under Asthma Remediation are warranted.
    ●   If a member has a “Y” indicator on the ESMF for this data field and the Social Care Navigator needs to
        learn more, the Social Care Navigator should ask the member: Did your household receive home
        improvement services under the NYS Healthy Homes Pilot? If the member answers yes, the Social Care
        Navigator should ask for additional details regarding the type/extent of home improvement services
        received and consider these in the context of appropriate Enhanced HRSN services from the SCN
        Program.
    ●   For guidance on how Social Care Navigators should identify potentially duplicative services, see Table 5-
        45: Waiver- and program-specific Social Care Navigator workflows, which provides program-specific
        instructions.

MLTCP/MAP Considerations:
    ●   For Housing - 2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications: If MLTCP or MAP are flagged on ESMF
        under MBR_LOB_Desc or if member verbally attests to program enrollment, the Social Care Navigator
        should ask for additional details for Housing services received. The Navigator should consider the
        member’s current services prior to referring them to additional Enhanced HRSN services. Member
        discussion should be noted in the member’s Social Care Plan.

Step 8. Confirm that the Medicaid Managed Care member wants to receive Enhanced HRSN Services for which
they are eligible and inform member of potential COI, if relevant
[[p.85]]
The Social Care Navigator should inform the member which Enhanced HRSN Service(s) they are eligible for and
ask the member if they would like to receive these services. If not, end the Eligibility Assessment.

In the event that the entity conducting Navigation (the SCN Lead Entity or contracted HRSN service provider)
navigates and also provides Enhanced HRSN services, members should be verbally informed of this dual role and
also be provided a statement about Freedom of Choice. Verbal statements should convey that members do not
have to use the SCN Lead Entity or HRSN service provider with dual role of Social Care Navigator/provider and
when applicable and available the members are provided options and member preference must be considered
first (see SCN Conflict of Interest Plan).

Social Care Navigators should document in the Social Care Plan that Freedom of Choice was verbally provided to
the member during the Eligibility Assessment.

Step 9. Complete a Social Care Plan that auto populates with existing member information and is tailored to
the Medicaid Managed Care member’s specific needs

Social Care Plans should automatically populate for Medicaid Managed Care members (see Social Care Plans).
Social Care Navigators should review and further tailor the Social Care Plan to support the member’s needs.
Member goals identified in Social Care Plans will be mapped to SNOMED Goal Codes by the SCN IT Platform (see
Eligibility Assessment Coding).

All historical member data within the SCN IT Platform system, including any initiated, partially completed, or
completed Eligibility Assessments, must be retained for at least ten years, unless intentionally changed or
deleted by the SCN Lead Entity or their contracted Social Care Navigators.

iii. Ending an Eligibility Assessment
An Eligibility Assessment will only be considered “complete” if all data elements specified as “required” in the
MVD and all associated resources specified as “required” by the FHIR IG are properly submitted in FHIR bundles.
Please view NYeC website section 1.10 for MVD specifics here: https://shinny.org/us/ny/hrsn/index.html.

There are specific statuses needed to ensure a finished and complete Eligibility Assessment including:

    •   Encounter Status=Finished
    •   Condition Status=Confirmed

iv. Situations in which a member does not respond to outreach for Eligibility Assessment
If the member does not respond to outreach from a Social Care Navigator to conduct an Eligibility Assessment
after identifying unmet HRSNs in the Screening, the Social Care Navigator is required to:

    •   Make at least three (3) outreach attempts within five (5) business days across daytime, evening, and
        weekend hours
    •   Conduct outreach activities across multiple modalities (e.g., phone call, text, e-mail)
    •   Document each attempted outreach in the SCN IT Platform‘s Social Care Plan
[[p.86]]
Social Care Navigators may bill for member and non-member facing time spent on the Eligibility Assessment,
Navigation, and Enhanced Care Management; however, time spent trying to reach a member will not be
reimbursed.

v. Considerations for children, youth, and households
Delivery of services to members in the same household: OHIP expects that SCNs help address the needs not
just of individuals but other individuals in their households where possible. Eligibility for Enhanced HRSN
Services is based on individual Screening results and individual Eligibility Assessments for each member within a
household. A member’s eligibility for Enhanced HRSN services is not impacted by whether other family /
household members are eligible or receiving Enhanced HRSN services, or by whether other family / household
members are eligible for Medicaid.

Social Care Navigators must work with members to understand who is part of their household and collect
documentation to confirm household members’ relationship to the eligible member. Members seeking to
receive Enhanced HRSN Services that would benefit dependents of the household must provide the Social Care
Navigator proof of connection to dependents in the household. Acceptable forms of documentation are tax
returns or legal documents (i.e., birth certificate, custody agreement, marriage certificate, court-ordered
parenting plan, mediation agreement, joint-custody affidavit). Social Care Navigators should work with members
to identify appropriate documentation and upload documentation in the SCN IT Platform.

Social Care Navigators must follow up to understand if other individuals in the member’s household are eligible
for Enhanced HRSN services. Social Care Navigators must document household size and other individuals
residing in a member’s home in the member’s Social Care Plan. Other individuals in the household may impact
how certain services are delivered (see Table 5-6 for additional details). SCNs must develop workflows for
tracking and billing for services for members in the same household. A household includes the eligible Medicaid
member(s) and the following individuals residing at the same residential address: their parent or legal guardian
(if the member is under the age of 18), their spouse or domestic partner (as defined in Section 2994-a of the
New York Public Health Law or any successor statute), dependents (i.e., individuals who are claimed or expected
to be claimed as tax dependents or by legal documentation), and children under the age of 18. Children include
adopted, biological, and stepchildren, as well as children under court or legal order establishing custody. Unless
the individual is also a Medicaid member and individually eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, the following
individuals are NOT included in a household: live-in aides, unrelated persons living together (e.g., roommates,
friends), additional family or relatives (e.g., aunt, uncle, sister, nieces/nephews), short-term foster children

Services delivered to a home (e.g., Medically Tailored Meals) must be delivered to a residence owned, rented or
leased by the member or their primary caregiver.

Household Enhanced HRSN Service Restrictions:

Service durations for Enhanced HRSNs services that benefit the entire household (e.g., rent and nutrition
services) are solely based on the primary eligible member. After the primary eligible member has exhausted
their approved service duration, different eligible MMC members within the same household cannot then apply
for the same Enhanced HRSN to prolong the service duration for the household. For example, if a primary
[[p.87]]
eligible member was approved to receive rent for 6 months, a separate eligible MMC member of the same
household cannot then be approved to receive another 6 months of rent service.

Children and youth residing in multiple homes:

   •   Delivering services to multiple homes: Dependent members under the age of 18 who are eligible for
       Enhanced HRSN Services and reside in multiple homes may receive services at each home of a parent or
       legal guardian in which they spend a considerable amount of time (this does not apply to homes of
       relatives and other adults). Enhanced HRSN Services provided to multiple homes must not exceed the
       per-member service caps outlined in the fee schedule where relevant (e.g., for Home Modifications).
[[p.92]]
        What qualifies as a considerable amount of time may vary based on the member’s living situation,
        needs, and the nature of services. Social Care Navigators should make a determination regarding which
        Enhanced HRSN Services need to be provided at multiple homes.

        During the Eligibility Assessment process, Social Care Navigators should do the following for members
        under the age of 18:
                o If member is under 10 years old, ask parent / legal guardian if the child spends a
                    considerable amount of time at multiple households
                o If member is 10 or above, ask the member or their parent / legal guardian if they spend a
                    considerable amount of time at multiple households
                o Document responses in the member’s Social Care Plan

    •   Documentation required: Before authorizing services at multiple homes, Social Care Navigators must
        obtain documentation confirming that a member under the age of 18 spends a considerable amount of
        time at multiple homes of a parent or legal guardian. Acceptable documentation includes but is not
        limited to a custody agreement, court-ordered parenting plan, mediation agreements, joint-custody
        affidavit, school registration that lists “address of record”, lease or rental agreement that lists the child
        as a tenant, food stamp documentation, general assistance documentation, or Temporary Assistance for
        Needy Families documentation. Social Care Navigators should work with parents / legal guardians to
        identify appropriate documentation and upload documentation in the SCN IT Platform.

    •   Billing services for children living in multiple households: For children in multiple households who may
        receive the same service on the same day (or date range) from the same provider at multiple
        households, the ‘concurrent claim’ modifier -76 should be added when submitting the claim. The
        modifier only needs to be added to claims beyond the first to avoid claims auto-rejection from MCO
        systems.

Additional considerations for HRSN Transportation services:

   •        For situations where a child/youth is eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, but their parent or legal
            guardian is not, NYHER will reimburse the HRSN transportation costs of one parent or legal guardian to
            accompany the child. NYHER will not reimburse additional HRSN transportation costs for additional
            non-eligible minors in the household.
   •        For situations where a parent or legal guardian is eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, but their
            children are not eligible, NYHER will reimburse the HRSN transportation costs for one minor if they
            need to accompany the parent / legal guardian (e.g., due to lack of available childcare).

Considerations for SCN service delivery for children in the foster care system

Children in foster care who meet requirements as outlined in Table 5-7 Enhanced Populations may qualify for
Enhanced HRSN Services. This includes:

    a. Children in family foster care home (i.e., temporary or long-term placements in a foster family’s home)
    b. Children or youth transitioning out of foster care (i.e., those aging out of foster care or reuniting with
       their family)
[[p.93]]
Note, children in congregate care (i.e., children in OCFS residential settings) are not eligible for reimbursed
Screening, Navigation, or Enhanced HRSN Services. However, SCN LEs should still form partnerships with
congregate care entities and, where applicable, establish workflows to assist with discharge planning.

Process to address unmet HRSNs for children in the foster care system

1. Children in family foster care home: In general, it is the responsibility of county and 29-I agencies to ensure
   the HRSNs of children in family foster care home are met, given that counties / agencies are required to
   meet the needs of children in family foster homes such as shelter, food, clothing, and transportation. Social
   Care Navigators should work with county and 29-I agencies to ensure that resources of county and 29-I
   agencies have been exhausted before children receive Enhanced HRSN services through the SCN program.

    During an Eligibility Assessment, the Navigator should determine and document if the child is in family foster
    care home by asking the child and / or their caregiver. If the child is in family foster care home, the
    Navigator should ask for the child and / or their caregiver for the foster care caseworker’s contact
    information.

    Social Care Navigators should then contact the foster care caseworker to ensure all county and 29-I agency
    resources have first been exhausted. If the child has needs beyond what county or agency resources
    provide, the county or 29-I agency should confirm with the Navigator that the child may receive services
    from the SCN program. The Social Care Navigator can then move forward with navigating the child to
    relevant Enhanced HRSN Services through the SCN program.

2. Children or youth transitioning out of foster care: During an Eligibility Assessment, the Navigator should
   determine and document if the child is transitioning out of foster care by speaking with the child and / or
   their caregiver. If the child is transitioning out of foster care, Social Care Navigators may move forward with
   navigating the child (and their family if relevant under Table 5-6 Household Guidance) to Enhanced HRSN
   Services through the SCN program. The Navigator does not need to engage with the foster care caseworker
   and does not need to receive a service justification from the county before proceeding.

vi. Considerations for criminal justice-involved individuals and justice-involved youth
OHIP recognizes that criminal justice-involved individuals and justice-involved youth are particularly vulnerable
populations, especially individuals with co-occurring conditions, who must maintain connectivity and access to
critical services and medications as they transition back to community settings. OHIP aims to ensure access to
care and improve outcomes for these populations, including through provision of Enhanced HRSN services such
as housing, food and nutrition, and transitional supports.
[[p.95]]
MMC members who are up to 90 days post-release from incarceration and have a chronic condition (including
but not limited to Substance Use Disorder, Serious Mental Illness, and hepatitis C) and high-risk justice-involved
youth (under the age of 18) with an identified unmet health-related social need may be eligible to receive
Enhanced HRSN Services through the SCN program (see Table 5-12: Enhanced Population Descriptions for
additional detail on eligibility criteria). SCNs are expected to conduct proactive outreach and support eligible
individuals within these populations to receive Enhanced HRSN services.
Per the Social Security Act (SSA) and the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (CAA), Medicaid is typically
suspended during incarceration (SSA) and then reactivated up to 30 days prior to release (CAA). Members are
initially reactivated into Medicaid FFS and then enroll in Medicaid Managed Care 30 to 120 days after release
from an incarceration facility. The timing of Medicaid reactivation may depend on the member's age, foster care
history, or whether the member is in a federal or state prison, a juvenile detention center, or a county jail.
Considerations for Criminal Justice-Involved Adults: Adult MMC members who are up to 90-days post release
from incarceration and who have a diagnosis of a chronic condition (including but not limited to Substance Use
Disorder, SMI, and hepatitis C) and an unmet HRSN are eligible for Enhanced HRSN services. OHIP envisions that
these individuals will:
    •   Receive HRSN Screening post release if Medicaid FFS is active so that they can be navigated to
        appropriate social care services based on eligibility. For example, a member can be initially screened as
        Medicaid FFS member after release either in coordination with the SCN LE or their contracted network
        (e.g. Health Homes) or by use of the self-screening tool on SCN LE websites and
    •   (Re)enroll in MMC once eligible in order to be able to receive Enhanced HRSN Services as appropriate
        during the 90-day window. For example, in coordination with the SCN LE network a Social Care
        Navigator could follow-up with the member and either assist with MMC enrollment if needed or if
        member is already enrolled in MMC, could re-screen the member as a MMC member and complete an
        Eligibility Assessment for potential eligibility and access to Enhanced HRSN Services.

OHIP encourages SCN Lead Entities to partner with jails, prisons, and Health Homes in their region to support
members to receive HRSN Screening upon release. Jails and prisons do not need to be included in the Network
(i.e., contracted with the SCN Lead Entity) but are essential SCN program partners.
SCN Lead Entities may take different approaches to accomplishing OHIP’s vision for this population, including:
    •   SCN Lead Entities may work with ecosystem partners to ensure that individuals are referred to the SCN
        for Screening in a timely manner following release (e.g., establishing relationships with discharge
        planners and/or case managers in order to ensure continuity of support for individuals)
    •   SCN Social Care Navigators may assist members in the transition from FFS to MMC by providing contact
        information for individuals trained in Medicaid enrollment (e.g., MCO enrollment counselors, NY
        Enrollment Counselors). Social Care Navigators are not expected to support members to fill out
        enrollment paperwork and forms
    •   SCN Lead Entities are strongly encouraged to include in their Networks HRSN service providers that
        specifically serve criminal justice populations and engage with individuals immediately after release in
        order to help them transition to MMC and also receive Screening
    •   SCN Lead Entities can support this partnership by providing materials (such as SCN program and contact
        information) for network partners to distribute to facilities, member, and member’s care team
        encourage outreach to Social Care Navigators upon release
[[p.96]]
Figure 5-4: Illustrative timeline of Medicaid re-activation post-incarceration

*Note post-release criminal justice population can only be offered Enhanced HRSN services if enrolled in MMC,
up to 90 days post-release from incarceration with a chronic condition.

Considerations for Justice-Involved Youth: OHIP is committed to strengthening the physical, mental, and social
well-being of NYS children and youth. Justice-involved youth are a particularly vulnerable population with
significant physical and behavioral health needs and challenges in access to care. OHIP aims to support high-risk
members of this population (see Table 5-12: Enhanced Population Descriptions for additional detail on eligibility
criteria) through Enhanced HRSN services to improve stable transitions out of prisons, jails, juvenile detention
and youth correctional facilities and promote improved population health and health equity outcomes.
SCNs are expected to work with organizations including juvenile detention and youth correctional facilities as an
ecosystem partner to meet the unique needs of juvenile-justice involved members. Juvenile detention and
youth correctional facilities do not need to be included in the Network (i.e., contracted with the SCN Lead
Entity).
SCNs will be expected to work with providers of case management services to support Screening and Social Care
Navigation for justice-involved youth after release from an institution.

sections.title: SCN Referrals
sections.text:
e. SCN REFERRALS

i. Referrals overview
Referrals to Enhanced HRSN Services are a core element of this program, wherein Social Care Navigators
connect eligible members to services, care providers, and community resources. These are Closed Loop
Referrals, meaning that when a member is referred for Enhanced HRSN Services, the Social Care Navigator will
coordinate the member’s connection to available resources and follow up to ensure services were rendered. In
order for SCN IT platforms to have Closed Loop Referrals, specific statuses and tasks must be used throughout
the referral journey.

This section outlines:

    •   SCN Referral Process: Programmatic process for how referrals are made to HRSN service providers from
        initial referral through service completion and referral closure
    •   SCN Referral Tracking: Data tracking elements to ensure accurate information collection
    •   Distribution of referrals across the Network: How Social Care Navigators distribute referrals among
        HRSN service providers

ii. Referral workflow with SHIN-NY data requirements
The referral workflow, from initial referral request through HRSN service delivery and referral closure, is detailed
below. Please also refer to the NYeC website for additional technical requirements for SCN IT Platforms to
integrate to ensure SHIN-NY data is accurate and processed: https://shinny.org/us/ny/hrsn/index.html.

Each SCN Lead Entity can specify its own standards for how a referral is sent, either as a:

    a. Direct referral point-to-point to an individual HRSN service provider, OR
    b. A general “broadcast” from the Social Care Navigator to the Social Care Network
[[p.98]]
“Priority” or “Urgent” needs workflows:

Social Care Navigators should be educated to determine priority and urgent needs of members on a case-by-
case basis when severe and immediate needs are identified through Screening and/or Eligibility Assessment. For
example, the Social Care Navigators must prioritize issuing referrals for members that are experiencing
interpersonal safety concerns as identified during the eligibility assessment. If the member wants assistance, the
referral must be issued as close to the same day of the eligibility assessment as possible. Additionally, when
Social Care Navigators receive an external referral for Medical Respite, the Social Care Navigator must prioritize
these referrals to ensure members are connected with an appropriate Medical Respite provider within 2
business days.

Navigation to existing local, state or federal services:

OHIP requires Social Care Navigators to utilize SNOMED descriptions per the Social Care Coding document and
update the FHIR service request to “Completed” after a member agrees to be navigated to ANY local, state or
federal service.

OHIP will require reporting accuracy for SNAP, WIC, TANF, local, state and federal housing assistance programs.
Please see Section k. Partnerships.

As a best practice, if a provider is on the SCN IT Platform to accept referrals for local, state or federal services
then the provider should utilize the statuses in Table 5-8 below.

iii. Referral to Enhanced HRSN Services
Step 1. Social Care Navigators are responsible for verifying the member’s Medicaid eligibility via MEVS on the
day of initiating referrals for Enhanced HRSN Services

Step 2. A Member may be contacted for service navigation if the referral is not being conducted in the same
visit as the Screening and/or Eligibility Assessment

Step 3. A member approves desire for service navigation or referral to Enhanced HRSN services

The Social Care Navigator will document the member’s consent for service and input notes into the member’s
Social Care Plan relative to their approved service(s) that will be visible to contracted organizations that accept
the referral for provision of Enhanced HRSN Services.

NOTE: After a Social Care Navigator verifies the member’s unmet needs, Enhanced Population, clinical criteria
and/or social risk criteria, then the Social Care Navigator should refer the member to eligible Enhanced HRSN
Services and move the referral(s) from “Draft” task state into “Requested”. Members should be referred to
eligible Enhanced HRSN Services even if the Social Care Navigator is waiting for proof of attestation or
documentation to support approving a referral for a different Enhanced HRSN service per Table 5-16: Eligibility
determination pathways for each Enhanced Population and Enhanced HRSN Service(s).

For example, a Social Care Navigator should proceed with sending a referral for Medically Tailored Meals for an
eligible member who has an unmet Nutrition need, even if the Social Care Navigator is holding back a referral for
Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications in anticipation of a provider attestation for proof of a physical
disability.
[[p.99]]
Step 4. A Service Request is sent to HRSN service providers or to service navigation and a copy to the SHIN-NY

Each referral will be associated with a specific Enhanced HRSN Service (i.e., members who are eligible for
multiple Enhanced HRSN Services will have a separate referral for each Service).

Upon receiving a referral for an Enhanced HRSN Service, the HRSN service provider can accept, reject, or not
respond to the referral (see Table 5-8).

Table 5-8: Required referral status changes for Social Care Navigators and HRSN service providers

The below statuses are used in data the SHIN-NY receives and may already be automated in the SCN IT
Platforms.

Technical considerations across HRSN service provider action options within SCN IT Platform:

    •   The timestamp of the referral being updated will be collected across all options of HRSN service provider
        responses to a referral
    •   Any narrative reasoning for rejecting the referral provided by the HRSN service provider in the referral
        Task does not meet FHIR standards and would not be transmitted to the SHIN-NY Data Lake

Step 5. The HRSN service provider accepts the Service Request through a Task
[[p.100]]
Step 6. The HRSN service provider contacts the member

Upon accepting the referral, the HRSN service provider conducts outreach to the member to initiate service
delivery. In many cases, the first step may be additional information gathering by the HRSN service provider (for
example nutritional information to inform Medically Tailored Meals).

If an Enhanced HRSN Service is successfully initiated by the HRSN service provider, the HRSN service provider
updates the status of the referral on the SCN IT Platform to “In Progress”. OHIP anticipates the Service Request
status remains as “active” for the duration of the “In progress” fulfillment status.

If during the course of service delivery, the HRSN service provider learns of another unmet HRSN that was not
identified during the initial Screening, the HRSN service provider cannot directly submit an additional referral for
relevant services. The member would need to be directed to their Social Care Navigator to be re-screened (and
member must be eligible for a Re-Screening) to be navigated to additional services.

If a member does not respond to outreach from the contracted HRSN service provider, either for an initial
conversation to initiate service delivery or after service delivery begins but before it is completed, the
contracted HRSN service provider is required to make the following outreach attempts:

    •   Make at least 3 outreach attempts within 5 business days (Note: attempting outreach alone is not
        reimbursable)
    •   Conduct outreach across multiple modalities (e.g., phone call, text, e-mail)
    •   Document each attempted outreach in the SCN IT Platform’s Social Care Plan

If the HRSN service provider is unable to initiate service delivery, the HRSN service provider is encouraged to
include a narrative reasoning for not delivering the service in the referral Task on the SCN IT Platform alongside
updating status to the relevant of “Cancelled”, “Rejected” or “Failed”.

Considerations for successful and unsuccessful initiation of Enhanced HRSN Services are outlined below.

Step 7. Then the Task can be updated to show this work is “In-progress”, this data is then sent to the SHIN-NY

If the member is receiving ongoing Enhanced HRSN Services such as Housing and Nutrition, their Social Care
Navigator should conduct outreach prior to Enhanced HRSN Service delivery completion (see Table 5-9 for
contact timeline expectations per received Enhanced HRSN Service). These contact points are intended to:

    •   Determine if Enhanced HRSN Services are meeting member needs
    •   Support in transitioning the member to additional supports after the end of Enhanced HRSN Service
        Delivery (e.g., existing federal programs), where relevant and desired. For example, if a member is
        receiving the Nutrition Enhanced HRSN Service of Fresh Produce and Non-perishable Groceries (Pantry
        Stocking), the Social Care Navigator should consider offering to transition the member to an existing
        service such as WIC or SNAP where applicable

Social Care Navigator engagement with members is a reimbursable activity under Care Management. Social Care
Navigator attempts to contact members (if member is not directly engaged) do NOT count as reimbursable care
management.

Step 8. Service marked as complete
[[p.101]]
When the service is completed, the HRSN service provider marks the Task to be “complete”, attaches a
procedure with a provision of service code, and the SCN Lead Entity marks the Service Request as “complete”.
Finally, a copy of this is sent to the SHIN-NY.

A completed service includes:

    •   Encounter Status=Finished
    •   Service Request Status=Completed
    •   Task Status=Completed
    •   Procedure=Completed

Step 9. Social Care Navigator conducts outreach after service completion

Within 5 days after completion of Enhanced HRSN Service, the member’s Social Care Navigator conducts
outreach to the member (see Table 5-9 for contact timeline expectations per received Enhanced HRSN Service)
to:
    • Confirm service delivery completion, and

    •   Support in transitioning the member to additional supports (e.g., existing federal, state, and local
        programs), where relevant and desired

The SCN Lead Entity, contracted Social Care Navigator, or HRSN Service Provider will update the status of the
“ServiceRequest” in the SCN IT Platform to “Completed” upon completing delivery of the Enhanced HRSN
Service. Updates to “ServiceRequest” and fulfillment request statuses are critical in downstream evaluation
including but not limited to milestone and metric calculations.

iv. SCN referral tracking
Enhanced HRSN Service referrals will have a coding status that follows FHIR standards, allowing relevant
member referrals and data to be to be transmitted to and from the SHIN-NY Data Lake. HRSN service providers
will have process tasks within the SCN IT Platform associated with individual referrals that will automatically
transmit relevant data from the QE to the SCN IT Platform such that the HRSN service provider has all necessary
information to complete the process task. Conversely, HRSN service provider activity in process tasks (e.g.,
updating a referral’s status to be accepted) will automatically be timestamped and transmitted from the SCN IT
Platform to the SHIN-NY Data Lake.

The Social Care Plan and associated data elements that feed Performance Metrics will be created and
automatically tracked during the referral activity.

    •   Data Reference: Referral Activities
    •   Data Output: Social Care Plan Creation, SNOMED Referral / Service and Goal Codes (required year 3)

Technical considerations:

    •   Referrals will be assigned an appropriate standardized SNOMED-CT referral code provided by OHIP;
    •   Each referral is a “ServiceRequest” by FHIR standards
[[p.104]]
The SCN IT Platforms must be capable of the following functionality and details in order to conduct and manage
Closed Loop Referrals and service coordination between SCN Lead Entities and their Networks:

    •   Track where a member was referred
    •   Refer to Enhanced HRSN Services
    •   Referral Status (see Artifact 4 & 5 of 1115 SHIN-NY FHIR Implementation Guide for specific referral
        statuses)
    •   Time to Closed Loop Referral
    •   Details on services delivered (e.g., type of intervention, duration)
    •   Service Begin Date: SCN IT Platforms must allow for Social Care Navigators to utilize date of 1st service
        provision to calculate the service duration period when applicable (e.g., 6 months of MTM is based on
        date of 1st meal provision to the member)
    •   Service End Date: The end of HRSN service duration
    •   Total Service Units Allowed

OHIP plans to have all referral data:

    •   Flow from the SCN IT Platform through the SCN’s designated QE partner to the NYeC/SHIN-NY data lake
    •   Track important information about the Network’s referral closure rate
    •   Address any unmet Medicaid Managed Care member needs

The SCN Lead Entity will be responsible for reporting this information and additional performance detail
monthly to OHIP (discussed further in Performance and Payment section).

v. Distribution of Referrals across Network
SCNs should strive to ensure a balanced distribution of referrals across organizations in the Network.
Organizations providing both Navigation and HRSN service delivery are required to follow their SCN’s conflict of
interest plan by providing members with a choice of which HRSN service provider they use. These practices
ensure SCNs operate in members’ best interests (see SCN Conflict of Interest Plan).

OHIP recommends Social Care Navigators provide multiple referral options to support member choice. However,
SCNs should monitor and track distribution of referrals to understand from whom members are receiving
services and to inform how SCNs can continuously improve.

sections.title: Service Re-authorizations
sections.text:
f. SERVICE RE-AUTHORIZATIONS

i. Overview
As a guiding principle, Enhanced HRSN Services are not intended to be permanent solutions, and Social Care
Navigators should work to connect members to more permanent resources (existing federal, state, and local
services) where possible.
[[p.105]]
Six services can be re-authorized beyond the initial 6-month service authorization:

    •   2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation
    •   3.1 Nutrition Counseling and Education
    •   3.2 MTM and Clinically Appropriate Meals
    •   3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions
    •   3.4 Pantry Stocking
    •   4.1 HRSN Transportation

For Enhanced HRSN Services that can be re-authorized, if a member is interested in receiving continued services,
a new Eligibility Assessment will need to be conducted (confirming Medicaid eligibility, Enhanced Population,
Social Risk Factors, clinical criteria, and duplicative services) and is reimbursable. If a member is determined to
be ineligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, the member can only be re-assessed within a 12-month timeframe if
they experience a major life event, as defined in the Operations Manual "Glossary of Common Terms” (e.g., new
symptoms or diagnosis, housing change).

ii. Social Care Navigator workflow for service re-authorization
Social Care Navigators should follow the workflow below to determine if members are interested in continuing
service delivery and if so, whether they are eligible to receive additional services. Social Care Navigators should
still confirm Medicaid MMC enrollment (via MEVS or ePACES) on the day of the new referral (see Figure 5-5). If
the member is determined to be eligible to receive continued Enhanced HRSN Services for any of the above
services, then a new referral must be created.

Figure 5-5: Service re-authorization workflow

iii. Additional guidance for re-authorization of Nutrition services
When a Nutrition service requires RDN/CDN approval (as specified in section 5.j.vi), members will need a new
nutrition assessment with an RDN/CDN upon re-authorization. As part of the re-authorization for Nutrition
services, Social Care Navigators should ensure the following as part of the Eligibility Assessment:
[[p.106]]
    •   That the member is actively enrolled in MMC via ePACES/MEVS day of re-authorization

    •   That the member is still part of Enhanced Population

In addition, Social Care Navigators should ask the following questions and document responses in the Social Care
Plan:

    1. Can you prepare and serve adequate meals either by yourself or with the help of a caregiver?

        •   If member answers “No” - refer to MTM or Clinically appropriate meals (based on eligibility criteria)

        •   If member answers “Yes” - Continue to question 2 below

    2. Would you or a caregiver be able to prepare and serve adequate, nutritious meals if supplied
       with ingredients and instructions?

        •   If member answers “No” - Refer to MTM or Clinically appropriate meals (based on eligibility criteria)

        •   If member answers “Yes” - Refer to food prescription, food vouchers, or pantry stocking (based on
            eligibility criteria)

sections.title: Enhanced Services Member File
sections.text:
g. ENHANCED SERVICES MEMBER FILE

i. Enhanced Services Member File (ESMF) Overview
The ESMF will be a core data source used in determining members’ eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services. It is a
data file referenced during the Eligibility Assessment to identify members who reside within an SCN’s region and
details their eligibility information. The ESMF will:
    • Include all Medicaid Managed Care members
    • Identify members who reside in the SCN’s region (see Medicaid Member Eligibility)
    • Assist the SCN in determining member eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services by identifying eligibility
         criteria from MCO’s member records (e.g., Medicaid High Utilizer, individuals with chronic conditions)
    • See Information included in Enhanced Services Member File for the full set of information contained
         within the Enhanced Services Member File

ii. Process for creating, sharing, and auditing the ESMF
Process by which the ESMF will be created: OHIP will provide a state-prescribed ESMF Template to the MCOs.
MCOs will then use the ESMF Template to:

    •   Create their own algorithm to query all plan members and associated HRSN eligibility criteria
    •   Populate template with all plan members and their HRSN eligibility information
    •   Report all plan members, including members with voluntary or involuntary disenrollment

Timing for sharing the ESMF: Refer to the most recent version of the DSIG for time frame MCOs have to
transfer the ESMF file to the RRHIO. MCOs will work with the RRHIO to remediate data quality issues by the 4th
of the following month. On the 5th of each month, the QEs transfer regional ESMF to each SCN.

Process by which the ESMF will be shared: Once NYeC/SHIN-NY receives the ESMF from MCOs:
[[p.107]]
   •   SHIN-NY will send a monthly ESMF to New York State’s Medicaid Data Warehouse (MDW)
   •   The QE partner will obtain the ESMF from the NYeC/SHIN-NY’s data lake
   •   Each SCN’s designated QE partner will subsequently send to each SCN an SCN region-specific Enhanced
       Services Member File
   •   SCN Lead Entities and MCOs are encouraged to create any additional data sharing agreements they
       deem appropriate to facilitate this information sharing

Figure 5-6: Process for sharing of ESMF

Process by which SCNs communicate to MCOs regarding new member information: During the Eligibility
Assessment, SCNs may learn new member information that may be relevant to MCOs per Table 5-16: Eligibility
determination pathways for each Enhanced Population and Enhanced HRSN Service. SCN Lead Entities and
MCOs will need to work together to establish a process by which SCN Lead Entities communicate this new
member information to MCOs.
OHIP will not require MCOs to update their ESMF data with information shared by the SCN Lead Entity.

iii. Information included in the ESMF
The ESMF must include all members enrolled in an MCO regardless of Enhanced Population status. See the latest
Enhanced Services Member File Template in the DSIG for the data elements and formatting requirements for
the ESMF.

sections.title: Changes in Member Medicaid Eligibility, Coverage and Relocation
sections.text:
h. CHANGES IN MEMBER MEDICAID ELIGIBILITY, COVERAGE AND
RELOCATION
It is possible that members may experience changes in Medicaid coverage and eligibility while receiving
Enhanced HRSN Services. OHIP aims to maximize member access to Enhanced HRSN Services while ensuring that
members receiving Enhanced HRSN Services are enrolled in a Medicaid Managed Care plan and meet eligibility
[[p.108]]
criteria requirements. The processes below are intended to support continuity of Enhanced HRSN services for
members covered by MMC plans in the event of a Medicaid coverage or eligibility change.

   For the purposes of this Manual, “members covered by a MMC plan” refers to all members who are actively
   enrolled in Mainstream MMC, HIV Special Needs Plans (HIV-SNPS), Health and Recovery Plan (HARP),
   MLTCP, or MAP.

ii. Change in member MMC coverage
If a member experiences a change in Medicaid coverage while they are receiving Enhanced HRSN Services and
the member is no longer covered by a MMC plan, SCN Lead Entities should aim to ensure this information is
communicated to relevant stakeholders (e.g., member, Social Care Navigator, HRSN service provider) upon
notification of the SCN Lead Entity. SCN Lead Entities are responsible for ensuring that delivery of Enhanced
HRSN Services to a member end when the member is no longer covered by a MMC plan. OHIP encourages SCNs
to support individuals who are not covered by Medicaid to access existing federal, state, or local resources.

Guidance is outlined below regarding (1) members with upcoming potential changes in MMC coverage (e.g.,
disenrollment from MMC), and (2) members that have experienced a change in MMC coverage.

1. Guidance regarding members with upcoming potential changes in MMC (e.g., potential upcoming
   disenrollment from MMC): Member Medicaid coverage is typically re-verified annually. OHIP recognizes
   that some members will therefore have to re-verify MMC coverage while receiving Enhanced HRSN Services.
   SCN Lead Entities should ensure that Social Care Navigators will:

      •     Check MEVS for the latest information during the Eligibility Assessment: When creating a Social Care
            Plan, Social Care Navigators should consider the members’ upcoming renewal and end date. For
            recurring services, the Social Care Navigator MAY (at the discretion of the SCN) refer the member for
            Enhanced HRSN service delivery only up until the renewal date / end date, or the maximum service
            duration end date, whichever comes first
      •     Consider a member’s upcoming renewal date: When authorizing Enhanced HRSN services, Social Care
            Navigators should consider the member’s upcoming MMC renewal date / end date. Social Care
            Navigators should make an effort to ensure services are delivered only to members that are enrolled
            in MMC with expected MMC enrollment through at least expected completion of Enhanced HRSN
            services (e.g., Home Modifications/Asthma Remediation)
             • Direct members to, or directly assist with, existing re-enrollment programs and resources to
               enable MMC re-enrollment (e.g., Certified Application Counselors, Marketplace Facilitated
               Enrollers and Social Care Navigators) if the individual has coverage through NY State of Health:
               Social Care Navigators and members can find the list of the over 5,550 statewide application
               assistors on the NY State of Health Website, which enables filtering of assistors by specific areas.
               For aged, blind and disabled individuals whose eligibility is determined by a local Department of
               Social Services, a Facilitated Enroller for the Aged, Blind and Disabled can assist in the application
               process. Social Care Navigators who have completed NY State of Health Assistor training may
               provide direct enrollment assistance to members to support MMC and FFS re-enrollment. Time
               spent assisting members may be billed to Enhanced Care Management for Medicaid Managed
               Care members and Navigation Services (Level 1) for FFS members. Social Care Navigators may
[[p.109]]
               provide direct enrollment assistance only if they have completed the required NY State of Health
               Assistor training and maintain all applicable certification requirements. Assistor certification must
               be renewed in accordance with NY State Department of Health requirements, and SCNs are
               responsible for ensuring that certified staff complete any required annual re-certification
               activities
             • Each SCN organization must designate a point of contact responsible for monitoring and tracking
               Assistor certifications and recertification requirements for staff providing enrollment assistance
               services
             • To provide enrollment assistance as an Assistor, the Social Care Navigator must be designated by
               the member within their account (via online or call center assistance) as their authorized Assistor
               in accordance with NY State Department of Health policies and procedures
             • Social Care Navigators are not required to directly support members with MMC or FFS re-
               enrollment (e.g., completing forms)

2. Guidance regarding members who have experienced a change in MMC coverage: OHIP expects that most
   members will be able to re-verify MMC plan coverage. In the case of a change in member eligibility (e.g.,
   member is disenrolled from a MMC plan), SCNs should establish processes consistent with the following
   OHIP guidance:
      • Verification of member eligibility in MEVS: SCNs are required to verify Medicaid eligibility in MEVS.
         SCN IT Platforms are required to have integration with the Medicaid Eligibility Verification System
         (MEVS) in order to verify Medicaid eligibility using one of the MEVS methods. SCNs were provided a
         deadline of August 31, 2025, for MEVS to be embedded within the SCN IT Platform to enable a direct,
         real-time connection to eMedNY. SCN IT Platforms are only required to support the ability to query
         MEVS to verify a member’s Medicaid eligibility at the time of service using a HIPAA-compliant
         270/271 transaction.
      • SCN communication expectations: SCNs are expected to create a process to quickly inform their
          Network HRSN service providers of changes in coverage of a member receiving Enhanced HRSN
          Services
       •     Delivery of Enhanced HRSN Services: The SCN Lead Entity and HRSN service providers are responsible
             for stopping delivery of services to members who are no longer covered by a MMC plan and thus are
             no longer eligible to receive Enhanced HRSN Services
                 o  Home and Safety Modifications / Asthma Remediation: if a member disenrolls from MMC
                    while their Home Modification or Asthma Remediation is underway, SCNs must end
                    provision of the Home Modifications / Asthma Remediation and return the member’s home
                    to serviceable condition. Services should not be provided while the member is not enrolled
                    in MMC
            • Supporting previously enrolled members: OHIP acknowledges that members who experience a
              change in Medicaid coverage may need support in finding federal, state, or local resources,
              reenrolling in Medicaid, or communicating with their HRSN service providers:
                 o   If a member is disenrolled from MMC and subsequently enrolled in Medicaid FFS, Social
                     Care Navigators will be reimbursed for Navigation supporting members to find existing local,
                     state, and federal resources
[[p.110]]
                o   If a member is disenrolled from Medicaid, a Social Care Navigator cannot be reimbursed
                    using waiver funds for providing Navigation services to the individual Social Care Navigators
                    may at their discretion connect individuals to other Navigation resources not supported by
                    waiver funds to access existing federal, state, and local services

iii. Member relocation and change of address
In instances in which a member moves across SCN regions during the course of Enhanced HRSN Service delivery,
OHIP aims for the member to experience minimal disruptions in service delivery while transitioning care to a
new SCN Lead Entity.

Updating member address: SCNs should proactively instruct members to notify their Social Care Navigator if
they are moving or plan to move. If a member’s address changes, the process for updating the member’s
address will proceed as follows:
    • Once aware of a member’s move, Social Care Navigators communicate address change with relevant
        MCO(s)
    • Additionally, the member’s address needs to be updated by LDSS or NYSOH – at whichever entity the
        member is registered for Medicaid. Social Care Navigators should support members in updating the
        member address with LDSS or NYSOH in a manner that best suits the member’s circumstances and
        needs and may bill time spent with the member to Enhanced Care Management
             o Social Care Navigators may work with members directly to help them contact LDSS or NYSOH to
                update their address; OR
             o Member can give live verbal consent to LDSS or NYSOH over the phone (e.g., three-way call) that
                a Social Care Navigator has authorization to speak on their behalf. Live verbal consent from the
                member is valid for 24 hours
             o Social Care Navigators may update member address themselves with LDSS or NYSOH as a
                member’s authorized representative (if a member is interested in receiving this support). To do
                so, members may submit an authorized representative designation form to LDSS or NYSOH to
                allow a Social Care Navigator to update an address on the member’s behalf. A Social Care
                Navigator may fill out the authorized representative designation form with input from the
                member, but must obtain a signature from the member before submitting the form to the
                relevant entity (LDSS or NYSOH)
             o If a member does not know whether they are registered with Medicaid at NYSOH or a LDSS, the
                member or Social Care Navigator may contact NYSOH at 1-855-355-5777 to determine where
                the member is registered
             o Additional guidance for NYSOH and LDSS is outlined below
    • As part of the transition of care, the member’s Social Care Navigator in the original region should
        coordinate with the SCN Social Care Navigator in the member’s new region to ensure the member is
        appropriately re-screened and able to continue receiving needed services as quickly as possible

Table 5-10: Additional guidance for updating member’s address

[[p.111]]

                                 directly, with either an authorized representative designation form
                                 completed or verbal consent directly from the member that the Social Care
                                 Navigator has authorization to speak on their behalf. The member will also
                                 need to provide their authentication information
                             •   Members can make updates in their online account at
                                 nystateofhealth.ny.gov. If members have an enrollment assistor, they can
                                 connect with the enrollment assistor directly in their online account to
                                 receive assistance
                             •   To update an address, the following data is needed: member first/last name,
                                 DOB, SSN, CIN, new address, and AC# HX ID
 LDSS                        •   Members or an authorized representative can go in-person or call their LDSS

                                 with either an authorized representative designation form completed or live
                                 verbal attestation directly from the member that the SCN has authorization
                                 to speak on their behalf
