ii. Health Equity Regional Organization (HERO)
United Hospital Fund (UHF) is the contracted HERO for New York State under the 1115 waiver and will be
charged with bringing stakeholders together to collaboratively support and augment public health, social
services, health-related social need services, data governance, data management, regional needs, assessment
and planning, VBP design and development, program evaluation and health care delivery for New York State’s
Medicaid members.

The SCN Lead Entities will each remain an independent entity that will participate with the HERO but are not
overseen by the HERO. Additional information about UHF can be found on the following website: UHF to Lead
Coordination of New York State Health Equity Regional Organization (HERO) | United Hospital Fund.

iii. Proactive member Screening outreach strategies
To meet Screening targets, SCN Lead Entities are expected to develop approaches to conduct proactive outreach
to members for Screening to maximize the number of individuals screened, particularly through partnerships
and collaboration with other organizations. SCN LEs should develop a proactive outreach plan which may include
a description of target populations, a roster of active partners and the role each plays in supporting screening,
priority geographic areas, chase lists based on the ESMF file for Medicaid Managed Care members that may be
eligible for Enhanced HRSN services, chase lists based on the MEF for FFS members, and plan for who will use
these lists, and planned outreach activities (e.g., text campaigns, school partnerships, etc.). Approaches should
include but are not limited to:
[[p.222]]
    •   Collaboration with Organizations: Working with organizations in the Network to offer Medicaid
        members the opportunity to be screened (e.g., identify and prioritize partners, formalize partnerships
        through MOU or a written agreement, engage partners regularly through check-ins and in person
        meetings, maintain an up-to-date partner roster to share with the network)
    •   Communication Channels with MCOs: Maintaining communication channel(s) with MCOs in the SCN’s
        region to direct member(s) to the SCN if the MCO identifies a member in need of Screening (e.g.,
        establish a designated POC for receiving MCO referrals, define referral intake standards, track MCO
        referrals, conduct regular check-ins with MCOs)
    •   Communication Channels with Providers: Maintaining communication channel(s) with health care or
        care management providers in the SCN’s region to direct a member to the SCN if the provider identifies
        a member in need of Screening, especially those who treat a large number of Medicaid members (e.g.,
        identify high-priority provider partners by focusing outreach on high Medicaid member populations,
        including FQHCs and community health centers, develop a clear referral pathway)
    •   Community Outreach Strategy: Developing an outreach strategy in collaboration with organizations in
        the Network to reach members in neighborhoods identified as having health disparities to encourage
        HRSN Screening (e.g., identify high-priority neighborhoods, design culturally and linguistically
        appropriate outreach, conduct outreach in different forms, i.e., in person and online, track community
        outreach activities, work with platforms to obtain data for chase lists, when needed)

Examples of SCN strategies for targeted outreach could include:

    •   Leverage “seek and screen” lists (e.g., based on ESMF per clinical criteria). SCN LEs are encouraged to
        coordinate with their SCN IT Platform vendor to obtain an aggregate ESMF file across MCOs. The
        aggregate ESMF list can then be filtered (e.g., asthma) and shared with contracted partners for targeted
        outreach attempts.
    •   Send tailored messages via text, email, and mailers
    •   Partner with organizations / entities who serve enhanced populations (e.g., work with behavioral health
        IPAs to reach members with SUD/SMI) and/or are in close proximity to enhanced populations (e.g.,
        nearest social care network partners and medical and behavioral health providers).
    •   Coordinate with MCOs’ care management programs serving enhanced populations
    •   Meet enhanced populations where they are (e.g., community events, back to school events)
    •   Consider paid advertisements via digital channels which can support audience targeting (e.g., YouTube,
        Facebook)

sections.title: Member Consent
sections.text:
l. MEMBER CONSENT
Consent to access and disclose data will be governed by SHIN-NY policies, which are intended to support access
to information beyond clinical settings, including the exchange of claims and social care data.
SCNs will collect and receive HRSN Data and other health data about Medicaid members at different stages in
the Screening, Eligibility Assessment, and Navigation process. SCNs will need to obtain consent from members
and keep members informed about their use of such information. OHIP envisions a consent process that focuses
on a meaningful and simple informed consent at each step for the member. In some cases, consent will be
documented and shared with the SHIN-NY, and in others, consent may be documented in the SCN’s IT System.
Consent processes across Screening, Eligibility Assessment, and Navigation / Referral are detailed below.
[[p.223]]
i. Member Consent for Screening
Any organization administering an HRSN Screen as part of the NYHER 1115 Waiver must capture member
consent as part of each Screening. The SCN must share the member’s consent to Screening with the SHIN-NY,
which will be documented as an answer in the Screening document itself.
Because OHIP will use Screenings for analytics and others will use Screenings to subsequently identify and reach
out to members who may benefit from HRSN services, it is important that members understand the potential
uses of their data. The consent explanation of the Screening should be easy to understand and not be a barrier
to services. It is important that members understand that their HRSN Data will be shared with the SHIN-NY and
will be available to their providers and Health Plan if they have consented to share their data in the regular
SHIN-NY manner.
Any member should be allowed to decline the Screening process in whatever setting it is administered. If a
member declines, the Screening does not take place.
Required use of Question 0: SCNs and any organization conducting Screenings on their behalf must use New
York State’s consent notice as “Question 0”, preceding other standardized AHC Screening questions. This notice
will clearly explain the purpose of the Screening. Member consent may be collected verbally and must be
documented in the SCN IT Platform. SCNs and any entities Screening using their native EHRs must use the
language below for Question 0:
REVISED CONSENT TO SCREEN (QUESTION 0)

We use this survey to understand needs our [members / patients / clients] have which could interfere with good
health. We may share your answers with your other health care providers, and with your health plan and social
services organizations, so they can determine if you qualify for any free non-medical services that could be
helpful. Please check this box if you agree to continue. You can choose not to answer this survey, but we can only
check for services if you do answer.

The lengthier the explanation in Question 0, the less likely it will be fully read and comprehended. However,
these additional sentences could also be considered depending on context:

ALTERNATIVE INCLUSIONS IN (QUESTION 0)

 •   You can choose to be screened later and may be eligible for extra services at that time.
 •   None of this will affect your ongoing Medicaid eligibility.

If a member is screened for unmet HRSNs using a platform other than the SCN IT Platform, members will still
need to provide consent for the sharing of Screening data (Screening Question 0) as part of the Screening in
order for the SHIN-NY to share the Screening data with the SCN Lead Entity to proceed with the Eligibility
Assessment. Please refer to section e.

ii. Member Consent for Eligibility Assessment
Following a Screening that identifies an unmet HRSN, SCNs will conduct an Eligibility Assessment. SCNs must
obtain member consent before proceeding with an assessment. For purposes of accessing other health records,
the consent will need to minimally include a brief explanation that a member’s health data will be used in the
[[p.224]]
process. Simple member education should be provided and may be included as part of a broader consent
process. For health data use purposes, approval by the member to proceed may be provided verbally and
documented.
At a minimum, verbal affirmation from a member is required to proceed with use of their health data. A
member should have the choice to say no and to stop the process from moving forward. The fact that a member
was given this opportunity must be recorded in the SCN’s IT Platform.
MEMBER “APPROVAL” TO PROCEED WITH ASSESSMENT

I would like to see, based on your medical history including information Medicaid collects and from Social
Services organizations, if you qualify for any services that could be helpful and which would be free to you. Is this
okay with you? Do you have any questions?

iii. Member Consent for Referral / Navigation
Before a SCN refers a member for an Enhanced HRSN Service, the SCN must inform the member that their
information will be shared with an HRSN service provider. The referral process should be described in a simple
manner, and the member’s affirmative verbal consent should be recorded in the SCN IT Platform. This consent
enables SCNs to safely transmit PHI to the HRSN service provider if the data meets the minimum necessary
criteria and is what a reasonable person would expect to be included.
Ideally, the SCN obtains consent to refer immediately following the assessment process while the member is in
person or on the phone. Otherwise, a follow-up to receive consent for referral could result in a delay in the
referral and subsequent service provision. Most importantly, the SCN’s workflow should prioritize ensuring the
members’ clear understanding of each step of the process. For a member, there should be no surprises in how
their information is used and to whom it is sent.
DRAFT CONSENT TO REFER

It appears that you qualify for [a service]. This service would be free to you. I’d like to refer you to an organization
that provides [this service]. I will need to send them some of your information. Is this okay with you? Do you have
any questions?

sections.title: Duplicative Services
sections.text:
m. DUPLICATIVE SERVICES

OHIP expects that services delivered by SCNs will supplement, not supplant, services that are already received
by members, including but not limited to existing state and federal programs and In Lieu of Services (ILOS)
provided by MCOs. Before authorizing Enhanced HRSN Services, the SCN Social Care Navigator must ensure the
member is not receiving duplicative services through other programs. Determinations of duplicative services
should be made at the service level and should not be interpreted as a categorical exclusion from SCN
participation based solely on enrollment in another program or a “Y” indicator within the ESMF. Members may
receive services through multiple programs simultaneously; however, funding may not be provided for the same
service type across programs. For example, if a member is already receiving Mold and Pest Remediation services
through another state program such as Healthy Homes, they should not receive Mold and Pest Remediation
services from the SCN. Social Care Navigators should assess the type and scope of services currently being
[[p.225]]
received and determine whether requested Enhanced HRSN Services would supplement or duplicate services
through other programs. This section outlines potentially duplicative services between SCN and other programs
(Table 5-44) and key components of the workflow that a Social Care Navigator should follow in ensuring services
are not duplicative for a given member (Table 5-45). Table 5-44 is intended to identify known examples of
potential service overlap and may not represent an exhaustive list of all possible duplicative service categories
or care coordination arrangements. See Table 5-15 as well for a view of how to consider duplicative services
alongside other eligibility criteria for Enhanced HRSN Services.

sections.title: Overall Approach to Performance Management
sections.text:
a. OVERALL APPROACH TO PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT
The SCN program will involve many organizations who have either not participated in Medicaid before or who
will take on new roles and responsibilities. As a result, as the program is launched, performance management
will be particularly important to ensure that issues and opportunities for improvement are quickly and
consistently addressed via a collaborative process.
Performance management will be a collaboration between OHIP and SCN Lead Entities. OHIP’s goal is to enable
timely and actionable improvements for SCNs to achieve 1115 Waiver objectives. Performance management
reports will help facilitate ongoing engagement between OHIP and SCN Lead Entities.
As part of the performance management approach, SCN Lead Entities will be responsible for generating specific
inbound reports (see SCN Reporting for additional details) both before program start and on an ongoing basis.
Complementing these SCN-generated reports will be a set of OHIP-generated outbound reports. These
outbound reports from OHIP will provide SCN Lead Entities with transparency into their performance (and peer
performance) and enable continuous performance improvement.
In addition to the planned reporting, SCN Lead Entities will be expected to submit real-time updates to OHIP to
enable timely assessment and management of SCN operations. The real-time updates include but are not
limited to network changes, governing body changes, and changes to SCN Lead Entity financials.

i. Performance Management Systems, Processes, and Validation
The SCN Lead Entity will report relevant performance metrics in accordance with detailed templates and metric
definitions provided by OHIP. Select metrics and reports are detailed in this Operations Manual, and others will
be outlined in additional materials provided at a later date. OHIP will review these reports to confirm accuracy
and identify potential reporting issues to resolve with the SCN.
Detailed Business Requirements (DBRs) for each relevant metric – including definitions of the metric, inclusion
and exclusion criteria, time ranges for reporting, etc. – will be provided to SCN Lead Entities in an instruction
manual, and relevant updates will be communicated as needed to ensure accurate reporting. Reporting
templates will also be provided to ensure consistent report format across all SCNs.
Inbound reports from SCN Lead Entities to OHIP will be submitted through an Excel sheet or other specified
format in the Health Commerce System or other specified submission process. Outbound reports from OHIP to
SCN Lead Entities will be transmitted through email attachment or Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) for the
SCN Lead Entity to access.
During the initial implementation phases, there will be a need for interim aggregate-level reporting before data
integration into the data lake is complete and as necessary systems, including vendor alignment, are
[[p.247]]
established. Early performance management reports will focus on basic operations and network composition
and then will gradually shift to include metrics focused on efficient operations, service excellence, and
benchmarking across SCN entities.
OHIP will review reports to confirm their accuracy and identify potential reporting issues to resolve with the SCN
Lead Entity. For selected identified metrics that are calculated by SCN Lead Entities and available to OHIP
through data aggregated into OHIP’s Medicaid Data Warehouse (MDW), metrics will be reviewed and cross-
validated to ensure accurate reporting. Any cross-validated metrics that have a significant discrepancy (greater
than 5-10% from original submission) will be flagged by OHIP and discussed during the performance
management meetings described below. The SCN Lead Entity will have an opportunity to resubmit amended
data in case of discrepancies due to error and/or other reporting issue.
Cadence of Performance Management Engagement: Performance management discussions will occur regularly.
OHIP may also request ad hoc meetings with SCN Lead Entities as needed. During these performance
discussions, OHIP contract managers will review monthly performance reports and discuss with the SCN Lead
Entities any identified issues and successes. Contract managers will support SCN Lead Entities with performance
improvement should performance concerns be identified.
Further Actions on Performance Management: Based on performance management reports and discussions,
OHIP may implement certain levers to support and assist the SCN, including tools for analysis, management,
data analysis, and consulting.
Additionally, OHIP will establish certain benchmarks for performance management metrics. If the SCN does not
meet the listed benchmarks, OHIP may provide short-term increased technical assistance to improve the metric
outcome. If SCN Lead Entities have consistent issues with performance management, OHIP may require
increased frequency of touchpoints between SCN Lead Entities and OHIP contract managers, and enhanced
analysis of SCN data.
For any performance management issues that the SCN does not have direct control over – such as HRSN service
provider operations or relationships with regional networks and other partners – OHIP may be able to provide
direct outreach to help alleviate issues. For direct SCN Lead Entity performance management issues – such as
internal data processing, staffing, or training / onboarding - OHIP will work directly with the SCN Lead Entity.

Select Performance Operating Report Metrics: OHIP plans to monitor performance using a set of key metrics.
Below are a set of proposed key operating metrics that may be used to assess SCNs on their performance
through monthly monitoring and reporting. The final list of metrics will be communicated to SCN Lead Entities
by their contract manager.
Metrics marked with two asterisks (**) are metrics also calculated by the SCN Lead Entity and submitted
through the Weekly Operational Indicator Survey. Those metrics not marked with an asterisk may be calculated
by OHIP and shared with SCN Lead Entities during regular performance management meetings.

Metrics

Member Engagement:
  • **Incoming member inquiries (#)
  • Outbound member outreach (#)
[[p.248]]
HRSN Screening:
   • **Members screened (#, %)
   • **Members screened on or off platform (#)
   • ** Members that decline consent (#, %)
   • **Members with a positive screen on or off platform (#)
   • Screening results by HRSN domain (#, %)
   • Screenings with complete demographics (% of Screenings)

   • Members re-screened within the year (#)
   • Members with an unmet HRSN (as determined by Screening) successfully contacted for an assessment
       within 5 business days

Eligibility Assessment:
     • **Members assessed (#, %, Retention %)
     • **Member for whom Eligibility Assessment outreach was exhausted (#)
     • Members assessed by HRSN domain (#, %)
     • Eligibility Assessment criteria response type by SNOMED/ICD10 Code (as % of Screens that identify an
          unmet HRSN)
     • **Individuals eligible for HRSN services who decline Eligibility Assessment (#, % of members)
     • Individuals eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services by Enhanced Services Population (#, ID’d by SCN)
     • Members assessed by clinical criteria (#, ID’d by SCN)
     • Members assessed by duplicated service (#, ID’d by SCN)

Referral:
    • **Members referred (#, %, Retention %)
    • **Members who decline referral (#)
    • Members referred by HRSN domain (#, %)
    • Members referred within 7 business days (%)
    • Referrals made that are accepted within 5 business days (%)
    • Social Care Plans created (#)
    • Referral backlog volume (# referrals outstanding TBD business days, %)
    • Referral follow-ups initiated by SCNs (#)
    • Referrals rejected by HRSN Service Providers (#, %)
    • Members navigated to WIC (DOH), TANF and SNAP (OTDA) (#)
    • **Members navigated to existing local, state and federal housing using SNOMED coding (#)
    • Members receiving Navigation for non-enhanced domains, by service type (#,%)
    • Members with identified unmet HRSNs in their Screening who are navigated to existing federal state,
        and local programs within 7 business days (%)

Intervention / Service Delivery:
    • **Members for whom a service is initiated (#, %, Retention %)
[[p.249]]
    •   Closed Loop Referral rate (% of referrals)
    •   Members with services completed (#, %)
    •   Members for whom a service is initiated, by HRSN domain (#, %)
    •   Members with services completed, by HRSN domain (#, %)
    •   Re-authorization of Enhanced HRSN Services (% of relevant Enhanced HRSN Services that are re-
        authorized)
    •   Accepted referrals for which a service is initiated within 2 business days (%)
    •   Members lost to follow up (# who initiate but do not complete)
    •   Members withdrawing from Enhanced HRSN Services (#)

Network:
   • **Size of Social Care Network (#)
   • **Composition of Social Care Network (#)
   • HRSN service provider utilization by Enhanced HRSN Services in region

Operational Efficiency:
   • SCN data submitted to QE within 5 business days (%)
   • Payments to HRSN service providers within 30 business days (%)

Metric benchmarks will be developed after SCNs begin to deliver HRSN services. Once established, benchmarks
will be leveraged to assess SCN performance relative to defined thresholds and to compare performance across
SCN entities.

provide a narrative report on their overall performance and relevant performance measures and tasks. The
[[p.253]]
Quarterly Performance Report will contain narrative on the progress made during the last quarter (including
Work Plan Performance Measures) and include a series of questions related to Objectives.

Report Metrics and Details: The Quarterly Performance Report will include SCN successes and
accomplishments, as well as any obstacles the SCN has faced and the steps they have taken to overcome
obstacles. Additional information will be requested for SCN Lead Entities to detail progress towards ensuring all
relevant trainings are provided to SCN Lead Entity employees, HRSN service providers, etc.

Submission Details: Submission deadline of 1 month after the end of each quarter (August-October, November-
January, February-April, May-July). Quarterly Performance Reports will be submitted using an OHIP-provided
Word template.

ii. Performance Management Report (Weekly Operational Indicator Survey)
Report Description and Objectives: This report contains numerous metrics aimed at assessing the impact of the
SCN program on members through Screenings, Eligibility Assessments, referrals, and HRSN services. Additionally,
select measures related to network and operational efficiency will be requested. The goal of this report is to
assess the extent to which SCNs are reaching and providing services to members within their respective regions
and to provide a pulse check to understand operational blockers.

If the organization serving as the SCN Lead Entity is the SCN Lead Entity for multiple regions, the Operational
Indicator Survey must be broken down by assigned region and not submitted as aggregate. A separate response
is required for each region.

Reporting Metrics: SCN Lead Entities are encouraged to work with their IT platform vendors and technical
analysts to provide the metrics requested. A set of instructions has been provided to ensure standard
submissions across SCN Lead Entities.

These instructions will contain definitions of the metric, inclusion and exclusion criteria, time ranges for
reporting, etc. SCN Lead Entities will be notified if any updates are made to the required metrics within the
Operational Indicator Survey. A reporting template will also be provided to ensure consistent report format
across all SCN Lead Entities.

Submission Details: Submissions are due by 12PM ET on Mondays for cumulative data collected since January 1,
2026 through 12PM ET the Friday prior. The Operational Indicator Survey will be due weekly beginning February
2, 2026. The first submission on February 2, 2026 will include cumulative data from January 1, 2026 through
January 30, 2026. Operational Indicator Surveys will be submitted using an OHIP-provided Excel template via

Report Description and Objectives: The purpose of the Governing Body Report is to define organizations and
relevant governing body members represented in each region.

It is acceptable if the SCN Lead Entity has a unique board for its overall organization that is separate from the
SCN Governing Body or modifies their current board to meet the requirements. There is no minimum or
maximum number of individuals for the entire governing body; however, SCN Lead Entities will need to follow
the minimum allotments and percentages per type of governing body participant.

SCN Lead Entities that were awarded more than one region (e.g., NYC boroughs) must indicate on their
Governing Body Report which Board member represents each awarded region.

After submitting the Initial Governing Body Report, the SCN Lead Entity will subsequently convene the governing

v. Infrastructure Cost Report
Report Description and Objectives: The SCN Lead Entity is required to submit an Infrastructure Cost Report on a
quarterly basis through Program Year 2 Quarter 3, and monthly beginning in Program Year 2 Quarter 4. This
report assesses expenditures across relevant infrastructure categories and includes a detailed checklist of
expenses categorized by type of spending. Additionally, it provides a summary-level Budget Statement and
Report of Expenditures (BSROE). This report will be used to monitor infrastructure funding spending and track
expenditures against the SCN's approved budget. Furthermore, it will also account for spending by CBOs related
to Infrastructure Capacity Building Funding.

Report Metrics and Details: Detailed expenses are broken down in expense checklists by type (salary,
contractual, travel, equipment, space & property, utilities, operating, other). These expenses by quarter and/or
by month will then be aggregated into the BSROE view to assess spend relative to contract period approved
budgets. Expenses will further be totaled by relevant infrastructure category.

SCN Lead Entities are required to report additional details on CBO Capacity Funding found under the Capacity
Funding tab. This includes the amounts of Capacity Building Funding awarded and allocated to contracted
501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) CBOs within the Network, as well as identifying information of the CBO and the uses of
funds.

Submission Details: Submission deadline is 1 month after the end of each quarter (August-October, November-
January, February-April, May-July) through Program Year 2 Quarter 3, and 10 days after end of each month
(June 10, July 10, etc.) beginning in Program Year 2 Quarter 4. The Infrastructure Cost Report will be submitted
using an OHIP-provided Excel template through specific SharePoint pages designed for each entity.

Contract managers will review the Infrastructure Cost Report for accuracy. Once the Report is approved, the SCN
will be contacted by their Contract Manager to submit a Claim for Payment. The Report must follow the Excel
template provided by OHIP, and it is important not to alter any formulas in the Excel file.

Member satisfaction is a key component of SCN performance and a priority of the SCN program. SCNs are
expected to solicit member feedback on a regular basis and at the end of service delivery, and commit to
continuous improvement to be responsive to member feedback. SCN Lead Entities will also be responsible for
responding to members’ complaints, in an effort to improve member satisfaction.
[[p.260]]

across all required questions.

Survey administration requirements
SCN Lead Entities must offer a member experience survey to each member (FFS and MMC members) within 30
days of the conclusion of their services (e.g., after a member received navigation to existing federal, state, and
local services, a home modification, or 6 months of medically tailored meals). In general, SCNs should send the
survey to members after the last service is provided (i.e., if member receives multiple services, send after
completion of the last service). SCNs must request consent from members to agree to participate in the survey
and permission to reach out for follow-ups.

Member survey design and implementation

    •    Survey audience and cadence: SCNs are required to solicit member feedback for members receiving
         services. SCNs are also expected to: gather feedback from members who only received Screening or
         Navigation, in addition to members who have received Enhanced HRSN Services; and gather interim
         feedback throughout a member’s journey, in addition to post-service.
    •    Survey channels: OHIP encourages SCNs to use multiple survey channels to increase accessibility and
         participation. At a minimum, this includes options for both synchronous (in person, via phone) and
         asynchronous (online form) survey completion. SCNs may consider mobile-friendly / chat-based
         interfaces if possible. SCNs are encouraged to leverage their IT Platforms to support survey
         administration, including to link member responses to demographic data.
    •    Inclusive and accessible surveys: Surveys should be designed and fielded in a sensitive, culturally
         appropriate, and accessible way. This includes but is not limited to using plain language that is clear and
         easily understandable and providing surveys in non-English languages (e.g., most commonly spoken
         languages among Medicaid populations in the region). Guidance for translating surveys is available here:
         https://www.ahrq.gov/cahps/surveys-guidance/helpful-resources/translating/index.html.
[[p.265]]
   •   Survey length and layout: Survey layout can improve response rates, ease of completion, and accuracy
       of responses. Wherever possible, surveys should:
                ▪ Be as brief as possible and cover only the most critical questions that will provide the
                   information SCNs need to improve member experience
                ▪ Segment surveys into multiple sections to demonstrate transition between different
                   question themes and break up survey length
                ▪ Maximize readability through simple language, accessible fonts, and ample white space
   •   Consistent training of survey administrators: Lead Entities should establish clear processes for how to
       administer the survey and should train everyone administering the survey on those processes. Lead
       Entities may want to provide instructions on the process steps to conduct the survey (e.g., providing
       guidance that phone surveys should start with a designated number of call attempts to reach member
       and end with documentation of engagement).
   •   Reviewing and acting on results: OHIP recommends that SCNs develop plans for collecting, analyzing,
       and reviewing on a regular basis the results of member experience surveys. For example, SCNs may
       convene a task force of representatives from the SCN Lead Entity and HRSN service providers on a
       quarterly basis to review results and develop approaches to action feedback. SCNs should look for
       trends in the data (e.g., for specific services or provider types, trends by demographic group) and
       develop action plans as needed based on member feedback.

Member satisfaction is a key component of SCN performance and a priority of the SCN program. SCNs are
expected to solicit member feedback on a regular basis and at the end of service delivery and commit to
continuous improvement to be responsive to member feedback. SCN Lead Entities will also be responsible for
responding to members’ complaints, in an effort to improve member satisfaction.

viii. Member Complaints Report
Report description and objectives: The purpose of the Quarterly Member Complaints Report is for SCN Lead
Entities to provide an aggregate quantitative summary of member complaints received by the SCN Lead Entity
related the SCN program. Complaints may be submitted either directly by a member or by a provider on behalf
of a member.

Report metrics and details: The Quarterly Member Complaints Report will include average number of business
days between complaint receipt and complaint resolution as well as the number of complaints by type of
complaint, by complaint source, and by complaint status (see Member Complaints and Reportable Incidents
Section for more details).

Submission details: Reports must be submitted within 1 month after the end of each quarter (e.g., August-
October, November-January, February-April, May-July), aligned with the Quarterly Performance Report.
Quarterly Member Complaint Reports will be submitted using an Excel template provided by OHIP.

Member Complaints and Reportable Incidents
Complaints may be filed by a member, their parent(s) or legal guardian, provider, or anyone else on behalf of
the member regarding the provision of services, activities, or benefits by the SCN program. Submitting a
complaint will not jeopardize a member's participation in the SCN program.

Table 6-10: Definitions of grievances, complaints, and reportable incidents

 Term                Definition

 Grievance           A wrong or hardship suffered (real or perceived), which is the grounds of a complaint
 Complaint           Dissatisfaction expressed verbally or in writing by or on behalf of a member. Complaints
                     can include, but are not limited to:
                     • Any violation of rights
                     • Availability of service or ability to receive service
                     • Quality of care received and/or whether services are meeting the member's needs
                     • Afforded choice of HRSN service providers
                     • Program eligibility and/or qualifications
                     • Whether health and welfare are being maintained
                     • Dissatisfaction with services or providers of services

 incident            health, or welfare of the member

SCN Lead Entity responsibilities: SCN Lead Entities are the first point for review and resolution of incoming
member complaints. SCN Lead Entities are expected to review and resolve member complaints in a timely
manner. OHIP acknowledges that SCNs will establish varied processes to address member complaints; a
minimum set of processes and timeliness standards are outlined below. As the first point of contact for member
complaints, SCN Lead Entities should receive all complaints related to SCN operations and service delivery,
including but not limited to dissatisfaction with Screening, Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN service delivery (i.e.,
Care Management, Housing, Nutrition, HRSN Transportation), Network capacity and access, and denial of
services.

Escalation to MCO or DOH: As appropriate (e.g., the SCN Lead Entity cannot resolve the complaint on their
own), SCN Lead Entities may escalate complaints to:
    • Member’s MCO: complaints related to member eligibility for services, or
    • NYSDOH OHIP Bureau of Consumer Services (BCS): complaints related to plan non-compliance
[[p.267]]
Complaints submitted directly to MCOs or OHIP: Consistent with existing MCO and OHIP processes, members
may also submit complaints directly to the member’s MCO or to OHIP.

OHIP may engage relevant SCN Lead Entities regarding member complaints it receives. In the event an MCO
receives a member complaint, the member’s SCN Lead Entity will be required to provide relevant information to
the MCO to address the complaint. MCOs should follow existing MCO approaches and guidelines for SCN
program member complaint review, resolution, and reporting to DOH.

In order to help ensure the SCN program addresses the needs of members, OHIP expects SCN Lead Entities to
report complaints to OHIP in summary form on a quarterly basis (See Quarterly Member Complaints Report).

Member complaint process
Expectations regarding informing members of complaint processes: During the Eligibility Assessment, Social
Care Navigators are required to verbally inform members how they may submit complaints to an SCN Lead
Entity. SCN Lead Entities should ensure that options for members to submit complaints are varied and accessible
and that members may submit complaints at any time.

SCN process to resolve member complaints:
Development of SCN Lead Entity plan for resolving member complaints: OHIP expects that SCNs establish
processes related to the review and resolution of complaints. These processes should include at a minimum:

   1. Process for how SCNs receive and review complaints
   2. Requirements for documenting receipt of a member’s complaint (e.g., name, address, phone number of
      complainant and location, date, and description of the complaint)
   3. Guidance for documenting the resolution of member complaints in the member’s Social Care Plan (if
      relevant)
   4. Resolution steps that will be taken to address a complaint, including but not limited to:
            o   Reviewing the details of the complaint
            o   Meeting 1:1 with the member regarding their complaint
            o   Sharing the resolution with the member
            o   Process to ensure that if a member is not satisfied with the resolution, the SCN must refer the
                member to their MCO

Termination of Member Services

SCNs must establish policies and processes for termination of member services that are aligned with the
following requirements:

As SCNs are engaged in the work of serving vulnerable populations and members with SUD, SMI, SED, I/DD and
other behavioral health conditions or members who require differing levels of support accessing HRSN services,
SCNs and their network must make efforts to meet members’ needs and assist them in obtaining needed HRSN
services in furtherance of the program’s goals. A member should only be terminated from receiving HRSN
[[p.268]]
services as a last resort, after de-escalation techniques have been attempted and the consent of OHIP has been
obtained.

Documented process for terminating a member:

Protocol for SCN staff and contracted providers to follow when a termination of member services is
necessary.

   o   Termination of services may be considered if an SCN has exhausted all attempts to assist the member.
       Termination may be appropriate where serving the member would cause an SCN or HRSN service
       provider’s staff member to be in danger or when the member engages in extreme harassment or verbal
       abuse against SCN staff or any of their contracted partners and de-escalation efforts have been
       unsuccessful.
   o   The SCN must alert OHIP of their intention to terminate a member and obtain OHIP’s consent prior to
       finalizing.
   o   The SCN should provide a full chronological contact log to OHIP documenting all member behaviors
       which justify termination and all efforts and de-escalation techniques employed by the SCN and its
       partner in their attempt to serve the member. The log should include, but is not limited to, the
       following:
            • Dates and times of problematic interactions with the member
            • Written communication from the member
            • Staff and/or contractors present during discussions with the member
            • Details on how the SCN attempted to serve the member including attempts to link the member
                to known behavioral health providers, MCO care managers, statements from contractors about
                their interactions with the member
            • General language or behavior the member used against the SCN or contracted entities that led
                to a termination decision including dates and staff and/or contractor responses.
            • Protocols followed to deescalate harassment or verbal abuse from the member and
                documentation of the written or verbal warnings provided to the member
            • Entity name and contact information the SCN provided to the Member about existing local,
                state or federal services that the member can utilize independently while termination is in
                discussion with OHIP or when finalized

OHIP requirements related to complaints: OHIP wants to ensure that members receive timely resolution for any
complaints submitted to SCNs. SCNs must meet the following standards related to complaint resolution:

   •   Contacting and updating the member within 72 business hours of receiving complaint
   •   Responding and resolving within 45 calendar days of receipt of the complaint

SCNs should report to OHIP a summary of member complaints on a quarterly basis. (See Quarterly Member
Complaints Report).

Member reportable incidents process
In the event a member experiences a reportable incident, SCNs must take additional steps beyond the standard
complaints process that account for the member’s adverse experience to reach a resolution. SCN Lead Entities
should ensure processes are in place such that the Network can meet the following timing requirements with
regards to reportable incidents.
[[p.269]]
•    The entity receiving a reportable incident (e.g., Social Care Navigator or HRSN service provider) must inform
     the SCN Lead Entity of a reportable incident within 24 hours of notification or discovery
•    The SCN Lead Entity must inform OHIP of the reportable incident within 24 hours of being informed about
     the reportable incident via email to SDH@health.ny.gov
     o In sharing the reportable incident with OHIP, SCN Lead Entities should include in the subject line
         “Reportable incident”.

OHIP will review the reportable incident submitted by the SCN Lead Entity and work in collaboration with the
SCN Lead Entity to resolve and communicate the resolution to relevant stakeholders, including the member,
HRSN service provider, etc.

7. PAYMENTS

Payments sub-sections:

a. Infrastructure Funding
b. PMPM Payments
c. Payment Methodology for Services Delivered
SCNs will be funded under the 1115 Waiver until March 31, 2027. The SCNs will have three main
funding sources throughout the three-year contract:
      1. Infrastructure funding: Funding to SCNs for operational setup of the program. SCNs will use
          infrastructure funding to build necessary functionality of the Network.
      2. PMPM payments: Payments for Screening, Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN Services will flow from
         OHIP to the MCOs and from MCOs to SCN Lead Entities. The MCO will make PMPM payments to the
         SCN by the 15th of each month.
      3. FFS payments for Screening and HRSN services: SCN Lead Entities will pay for Screening,
         Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN Services delivered according to a set HRSN fee schedule.

Figure 7-1: Overview of payment flows included in SCN program
[[p.271]]
For the Medicaid FFS population, the SCN Lead Entity will directly bill eMedNY for Screening and
Navigation for the region’s Medicaid FFS population. The SCN Lead Entity will use the PMPM Payment
to provide the Network with payments for Screening, Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN Services for the
Medicaid Managed Care population.

After the 1115 Waiver period, a subsequent payment mechanism may be established and is beyond the scope of
the current program. SCNs may continue to receive funding from state, federal, or private grants during and
after the initial three-year contract period.

The following section provides an overview of each type of payment within the 1115 Waiver, including
funding amount and mechanics details, uses of funding, and funding requirements.

sections.title: Infrastructure Funding
sections.text:
a. INFRASTRUCTURE FUNDING

i. Funding amount and mechanics
To ensure that SCNs are able to build capacity and capabilities, OHIP is providing up to $500 million in federal
infrastructure funding for the operational setup of the program across the three-year RFA period. SCN Lead
Entities may use infrastructure funding to build necessary functionality and capabilities across the Network,
either through direct use of funds for activities impacting capabilities of the Network, or via capacity building
grants provided to CBOs.

The maximum infrastructure funding available for each SCN varies by region and is based on the number of
Medicaid members and cost of delivering HRSN services in its region. OHIP has communicated to each SCN Lead
Entity the maximum funding amount available in each year. SCN Lead Entities are required to keep receipts,
records, and other financial documents related to the federal infrastructure funding including CBO Capacity
Funding for the balance of each calendar year in which they were made and for six (6) additional years
thereafter.

While OHIP’s goal is to ensure that all SCNs receive the maximum amount of infrastructure funding, SCNs will be
expected to provide reports and achieve certain operational and performance milestones in order to receive
their maximum amount of infrastructure funding. These contingencies are intended to incentivize SCNs to
prioritize critical operational and performance goals, as well as prepare SCNs for more robust value-based
payment models in the future. Payment will be contingent on three types of requirements:

            1. Submitting required reports
            2. Completing key implementation milestones
            3. Achieving performance targets

OHIP will issue a 25% advance of Year 1 infrastructure funding immediately after SCNs execute their contracts
with OHIP, and funding will be paid on a quarterly basis thereafter. The 25% advance funding is subject to
recoupment every quarter.

SCN Lead Entities will receive the majority of their infrastructure funding beyond the advance retrospectively
after the milestones and targets are reached and reports are submitted.
[[p.272]]
ii. Uses of funding
SCNs will use infrastructure funding to build necessary functionality across the Network, including but not
limited to initial Network infrastructure set-up (e.g., onboarding of CBOs), initial set-up and implementation of
the SCN IT Platform, hiring and recruiting of staff, CBO capacity building activities and technical assistance,
contracting, and community and health care provider engagement. Infrastructure funds cannot be used for EHR
interoperability integration (e.g., API to connect EHR to SCN IT platform).

SCNs may rollover unspent funds from quarter to quarter, subject to the spending minimum detailed below.

OHIP will collect the SCN Lead Entities’ estimated infrastructure budget proposal for each year based on the
Annual Infrastructure Reassessment Report and will require SCN Lead Entities to report their expenditures on a
quarterly basis.

iii. Funding requirements
Each quarterly payment will be split into portions tied to reporting requirements, implementation milestone
requirements, and performance requirements. If an SCN fails to meet any of these requirements in a given
quarter, it will not receive the funding tied to that requirement for that quarter. The funding amounts tied to
each requirement type in each quarter are shown in Table 7-2.
[[p.273]]

performance
